   146→
   147→def _append_reorganize_actions(
   148→    actions: list[ActionItem],
   149→    by_detector: dict[str, int],
   150→    impact_for: Callable[[str, int], float],
   151→) -> None:
   152→    """Append structure/move oriented actions."""
   153→    for detector, tool_info in DETECTOR_TOOLS.items():
   154→        if tool_info["action_type"] != "reorganize":
   155→            continue
   156→        count = by_detector.get(detector, 0)
   157→        if count == 0:
   158→            continue
   159→
   160→        guidance = tool_info.get("guidance", "restructure with move")
   161→        actions.append(
   162→            {
   163→                "type": "reorganize",
   164→                "detector": detector,
   165→                "count": count,
   166→                "description": f"{count} {detector} findings — {guidance}",
   167→                "command": f"desloppify show {detector} --status open",
   168→                "impact": round(impact_for(detector, count), 1),
   169→                "dimension": _dimension_name(detector),
   170→            }
   171→        )
   172→
   173→
   174→def _build_refactor_entry(
   175→    detector: str,
   176→    tool_info: dict[str, Any],
   177→    count: int,
   178→    impact_for: Callable[[str, int], float],
   179→) -> ActionItem:
   180→    """Build one refactor/manual action row."""
   181→    guidance = tool_info.get("guidance", "manual fix")
   182→    adjusted_info = {**tool_info, "guidance": guidance}
   183→
   184→    if detector == "subjective_review":
   185→        command = "desloppify review --prepare"
   186→        description = f"{count} files need design review — run holistic review to refresh subjective scores"
   187→    elif detector == "review":
   188→        command = "desloppify show review --status open"
   189→        suffix = "s" if count != 1 else ""
   190→        description = (
   191→            f"{count} review finding{suffix} need investigation — "
   192→            "run `desloppify show review --status open` to see them"
   193→        )
   194→        adjusted_info = {**adjusted_info, "action_type": "refactor"}
   195→    else:
   196→        command = f"desloppify show {detector} --status open"
   197→        description = f"{count} {detector} findings — {guidance}"
   198→
   199→    return {
   200→        "type": adjusted_info["action_type"],
   201→        "detector": detector,
   202→        "count": count,
   203→        "description": description,
   204→        "command": command,
   205→        "impact": round(impact_for(detector, count), 1),
   206→        "dimension": _dimension_name(detector),
   207→    }
   208→
   209→
   210→def _append_refactor_actions(
   211→    actions: list[ActionItem],
   212→    by_detector: dict[str, int],
   213→    impact_for: Callable[[str, int], float],
   214→) -> None:
   215→    """Append refactor/manual actions after auto-fix/reorg buckets."""
   216→    for detector, tool_info in DETECTOR_TOOLS.items():
   217→        if tool_info["action_type"] not in {"refactor", "manual_fix"}:
   218→            continue
   219→        count = by_detector.get(detector, 0)
   220→        if count == 0:
   221→            continue
   222→        actions.append(_build_refactor_entry(detector, tool_info, count, impact_for))
   223→
   224→
   225→def _append_debt_action(actions: list[ActionItem], debt: dict[str, float]) -> None:
   226→    """Append wontfix-debt callout when gap is material."""
   227→    gap = float(debt.get("overall_gap", 0.0) or 0.0)
   228→    if gap <= 2.0:
   229→        return
   230→    actions.append(
   231→        {
   232→            "type": "debt_review",
   233→            "detector": None,
   234→            "description": f"{gap} pts of wontfix debt — review stale decisions",
   235→            "command": "desloppify show --status wontfix",
   236→            "gap": gap,
   237→        }
   238→    )
   239→
   240→
   241→def _assign_priorities(actions: list[ActionItem]) -> list[ActionItem]:
   242→    """Sort and assign sequential priorities."""
   243→    type_order = {
   244→        "issue_queue": 0,
   245→        "auto_fix": 1,
   246→        "reorganize": 2,
   247→        "refactor": 3,
   248→        "manual_fix": 4,
   249→        "debt_review": 5,
   250→    }
   251→    actions.sort(
   252→        key=lambda action: (type_order.get(action["type"], 9), -action.get("impact", 0))
   253→    )
   254→    for index, action in enumerate(actions, start=1):
   255→        action["priority"] = index
   256→    return actions
   257→
   258→
   259→def _cluster_detector(cluster: dict) -> str | None:
   260→    """Extract the primary detector from a cluster.
   261→
   262→    Uses the cluster_key prefix (e.g. "auto::unused" → "unused",
   263→    "typed::dict_keys::phantom_read" → "dict_keys") or falls back
   264→    to the first member's detector.
   265→    """
   266→    key = cluster.get("cluster_key", "")
   267→    if key:
   268→        parts = key.split("::")
   269→        if len(parts) >= 2:
   270→            return parts[1]
   271→    # Fallback: parse from cluster name (auto/detector-subtype)
   272→    name = cluster.get("name", "")
   273→    if name.startswith("auto/"):
   274→        rest = name[5:]
   275→        return rest.split("-", 1)[0] if "-" in rest else rest
   276→    return None
   277→
   278→
   279→def _annotate_with_clusters(
   280→    actions: list[ActionItem], clusters: dict | None
   281→) -> None:
   282→    """Annotate actions with matching cluster info when clusters exist."""
   283→    if not clusters:
   284→        return
   285→    for action in actions:
   286→        detector = action.get("detector")
   287→        if not detector:
   288→            continue
   289→        matching = [
   290→            name
   291→            for name, c in clusters.items()
   292→            if c.get("auto") and _cluster_detector(c) == detector
   293→        ]
   294→        if matching:
   295→            action["clusters"] = matching
   296→            action["cluster_count"] = len(matching)
   297→            action["command"] = "desloppify next"
   298→            count = action.get("count", 0)
   299→            display = action.get("detector", "unknown")
   300→            action["description"] = (
   301→                f"{count} {display} findings in {len(matching)} cluster(s) — "
   302→                f"run `desloppify next`"
   303→            )
   304→
   305→
   306→def compute_actions(ctx: ActionContext) -> list[ActionItem]:
   307→    """Compute prioritized action list with tool mapping."""
   308→    actions: list[ActionItem] = []
   309→    impact_for = _impact_calculator(ctx.dimension_scores, ctx.state)
   310→    supported = supported_fixers(ctx.state, ctx.lang)
   311→
   312→    _append_auto_fix_actions(actions, ctx.by_detector, supported, impact_for, ctx.state)
   313→    _append_reorganize_actions(actions, ctx.by_detector, impact_for)
   314→    _append_refactor_actions(actions, ctx.by_detector, impact_for)
   315→    _append_debt_action(actions, ctx.debt)
   316→
   317→    prioritized = _assign_priorities(actions)
   318→    _annotate_with_clusters(prioritized, ctx.clusters)
   319→    return prioritized
   320→

     5→LOW_SCORE_FINDING_THRESHOLD = 85.0
     6→ASSESSMENT_FEEDBACK_THRESHOLD = 100.0

    19→def max_batch_findings_for_dimension_count(dimension_count: int) -> int:
    20→    """Return the normalized max findings budget for one batch payload."""
    21→    safe_count = max(0, int(dimension_count))
    22→    return max(DEFAULT_MAX_BATCH_FINDINGS, safe_count)

    25→def score_requires_dimension_finding(score: float) -> bool:

    27→    return float(score) < LOW_SCORE_FINDING_THRESHOLD
    28→
    29→
    30→def score_requires_explicit_feedback(score: float) -> bool:
    31→    """Return True when score requires a finding or dimension-note evidence."""
    32→    return float(score) < ASSESSMENT_FEEDBACK_THRESHOLD
    33→
    34→
    35→def global_prompt_contract() -> str:
    36→    """Render shared review contract text injected into all review prompts."""
    37→    return (
    38→        f"{_PROMPT_CONTRACT_HEADER}\n"
    39→        "- Scope breadth: report any material issues supported by evidence "
    40→        "(structural, architectural, boundary, readability, lifecycle), "
    41→        "not only low-level nits.\n"
    42→        "- Dimension boundaries are guidance, not a gag-order: if an issue "
    43→        "spans dimensions, report it under the most impacted dimension.\n"
    44→        "- Do not default to 100. Reserve 100 for genuinely exemplary code "
    45→        "with clear positive evidence; if there is uncertainty or residual "
    46→        "issues, score below 100.\n"
    47→        "- Do not suppress valid findings to keep scores high.\n"
    48→        f"- Scores below {LOW_SCORE_FINDING_THRESHOLD:.1f} MUST include at least one "
    49→        "finding for that same dimension.\n"
    50→        f"- Scores below {ASSESSMENT_FEEDBACK_THRESHOLD:.1f} MUST include explicit "
    51→        "feedback for that same dimension (finding with suggestion or "
    52→        "dimension_notes evidence).\n"
    53→        f"- Scores above {HIGH_SCORE_ISSUES_NOTE_THRESHOLD:.1f} MUST include a "
    54→        "non-empty `issues_preventing_higher_score` note for that dimension.\n"
    55→        "- Findings must always describe defects that need change, never positive observations.\n"
    56→        "- Think structurally: when individual findings form a pattern, consider what is\n"
    57→        "  causing them. If several issues stem from a shared root cause (missing abstraction,\n"
    58→        "  repeated pattern, inconsistent convention), say so in the findings — explain the\n"
    59→        "  deeper issue and use root_cause_cluster to connect related symptoms."
    60→    )
    61→

    63→def ensure_prompt_contract(system_prompt: str) -> str:

    66→    if _PROMPT_CONTRACT_HEADER in text:

    68→    suffix = global_prompt_contract()
    69→    if not text:
    70→        return suffix
    71→    return f"{text}\n\n{suffix}"

    26→def select_holistic_files(path: Path, lang: object, files: list[str] | None) -> list[str]:
    27→    selected = files if files is not None else (lang.file_finder(path) if lang.file_finder else [])
    28→    if not selected:

    30→

    39→            zone_value = getattr(zone, "value", str(zone))
    40→        except (AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
    41→            zone_value = "production"

    58→    top_imported = sorted(importer_counts.items(), key=lambda item: -item[1])[:10]
    59→    arch["god_modules"] = [

    73→            stripped = raw_line.strip()
    74→            if stripped.startswith(
    75→                ("def ", "class ", "async def ", "if ", "#", "@", "import ", "from ")
    76→            ):
    77→                continue
    78→            if re.search(
    79→                r"\b(?:open|connect|requests?\.|urllib|subprocess|os\.system)\b",
    80→                stripped,
    81→            ):
    82→                module_level_io.append(
    83→                    {
    84→                        "file": rel(filepath),
    85→                        "line": idx + 1,
    86→                        "code": stripped[:100],
    87→                    }
    88→                )
    89→    if module_level_io:
    90→        coupling["module_level_io"] = module_level_io[:20]
    91→    return coupling
    92→
    93→
    94→def _naming_conventions_context(file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:
    95→    dir_styles: dict[str, Counter] = {}
    96→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
    97→        parts = Path(filepath).parts
    98→        if len(parts) < 2:
    99→            continue
   100→        dir_name = parts[-2] + "/"
   101→        counter = dir_styles.setdefault(dir_name, Counter())
   102→        for name in _FUNC_NAME_RE.findall(content):
   103→            if "_" in name and name.islower():
   104→                counter["snake_case"] += 1
   105→            elif name[0].islower() and any(ch.isupper() for ch in name):
   106→                counter["camelCase"] += 1
   107→            elif name[0].isupper():
   108→                counter["PascalCase"] += 1
   109→    return {
   110→        name: dict(counter.most_common(3))
   111→        for name, counter in dir_styles.items()
   112→        if sum(counter.values()) >= 3
   113→    }
   114→
   115→
   116→def _sibling_behavior_context(
   117→    file_contents: dict[str, str], *, base_path: Path | str | None = None
   118→) -> dict:
   119→    root = Path(base_path).resolve() if base_path is not None else None
   120→
   121→    def _bucket_for(filepath: str) -> str | None:
   122→        target = Path(filepath).resolve()
   123→        if root is not None:
   124→            try:
   125→                parts = target.relative_to(root).parts
   126→                if len(parts) >= 2:
   127→                    return f"{parts[0]}/"
   128→                return None
   129→            except ValueError:
   130→                logger.debug("Path %s not relative to root %s, using fallback bucket", filepath, root)
   131→        parts = Path(filepath).parts
   132→        if len(parts) < 2:
   133→            return None
   134→        return f"{parts[-2]}/"
   135→
   136→    def _display_path(filepath: str) -> str:
   137→        target = Path(filepath).resolve()
   138→        if root is not None:
   139→            try:
   140→                return target.relative_to(root).as_posix()
   141→            except ValueError:
   142→                logger.debug("Path %s not relative to root %s, using rel() fallback", filepath, root)
   143→        return rel(filepath)
   144→
   145→    dir_imports: dict[str, dict[str, set[str]]] = {}
   146→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
   147→        dir_name = _bucket_for(filepath)
   148→        if dir_name is None:
   149→            continue
   150→        file_rel = _display_path(filepath)
   151→        dir_imports.setdefault(dir_name, {})[file_rel] = _extract_imported_names(content)
   152→
   153→    sibling_behavior: dict = {}
   154→    for dir_name, file_names_map in dir_imports.items():
   155→        total = len(file_names_map)
   156→        if total < 3:
   157→            continue
   158→        name_counts: Counter = Counter()
   159→        for names in file_names_map.values():
   160→            for name in names:
   161→                name_counts[name] += 1
   162→        threshold = total * 0.6
   163→        shared = {
   164→            name: count for name, count in name_counts.items() if count >= threshold
   165→        }
   166→        if not shared:
   167→            continue
   168→        outliers = []
   169→        for file_rel, names in file_names_map.items():
   170→            missing = [name for name in shared if name not in names]
   171→            if missing:
   172→                outliers.append({"file": file_rel, "missing": sorted(missing)})
   173→        if not outliers:
   174→            continue
   175→        sibling_behavior[dir_name] = {
   176→            "shared_patterns": {
   177→                name: {"count": count, "total": total}
   178→                for name, count in sorted(shared.items(), key=lambda item: -item[1])
   179→            },
   180→            "outliers": sorted(
   181→                outliers, key=lambda item: len(item["missing"]), reverse=True
   182→            ),
   183→        }
   184→    return sibling_behavior
   185→
   186→
   187→def _error_strategy_context(file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:
   188→    dir_errors: dict[str, Counter] = {}
   189→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
   190→        parts = Path(filepath).parts
   191→        if len(parts) < 2:
   192→            continue
   193→        dir_name = parts[-2] + "/"
   194→        counter = dir_errors.setdefault(dir_name, Counter())
   195→        for pattern_name, pattern in _ERROR_PATTERNS.items():
   196→            matches = pattern.findall(content)
   197→            if matches:
   198→                counter[pattern_name] += len(matches)
   199→    return {
   200→        name: dict(counter.most_common(5))
   201→        for name, counter in dir_errors.items()
   202→        if sum(counter.values()) >= 2
   203→    }
   204→
   205→
   206→def _in_allowed_files(filepath: object, allowed_files: set[str] | None) -> bool:
   207→    if allowed_files is None:
   208→        return True
   209→    return isinstance(filepath, str) and filepath in allowed_files
   210→
   211→
   212→def _dependencies_context(
   213→    state: dict,
   214→    *,
   215→    allowed_files: set[str] | None = None,
   216→) -> dict:
   217→    cycle_findings = []
   218→    cycle_files: list[str] = []
   219→    cycle_edges: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   220→    seen_cycle_files: set[str] = set()
   221→    findings = state.get("findings", {})
   222→    if not isinstance(findings, dict):
   223→        findings = {}
   224→    for finding in findings.values():
   225→        if not isinstance(finding, dict):
   226→            continue
   227→        if finding.get("detector") != "cycles" or finding.get("status") != "open":
   228→            continue
   229→        if not _in_allowed_files(finding.get("file", ""), allowed_files):
   230→            continue
   231→        cycle_findings.append(finding)
   232→        detail = finding.get("detail", {})
   233→        if isinstance(detail, dict):
   234→            raw_cycle_paths = detail.get("files", [])
   235→            normalized_paths: list[str] = []
   236→            if isinstance(raw_cycle_paths, list):
   237→                for raw_path in raw_cycle_paths:
   238→                    if not isinstance(raw_path, str):
   239→                        continue
   240→                    path = raw_path.strip()
   241→                    if not path:
   242→                        continue
   243→                    normalized_paths.append(path)
   244→                    if path in seen_cycle_files:
   245→                        continue
   246→                    seen_cycle_files.add(path)
   247→                    cycle_files.append(path)
   248→            if normalized_paths:
   249→                raw_length = detail.get("length")
   250→                length = (
   251→                    int(raw_length)
   252→                    if isinstance(raw_length, int | float)
   253→                    else len(normalized_paths)
   254→                )
   255→                cycle_edges.append({"files": normalized_paths, "length": max(1, length)})
   256→    if not cycle_findings:
   257→        return {}
   258→    return {
   259→        "existing_cycles": len(cycle_findings),
   260→        "cycle_summaries": [
   261→            str(finding.get("summary", "")).strip()[:120]
   262→            for finding in cycle_findings[:10]
   263→            if str(finding.get("summary", "")).strip()
   264→        ],
   265→        "cycle_files": cycle_files[:40],
   266→        "cycle_edges": cycle_edges[:10],
   267→    }
   268→
   269→
   270→def _testing_context(
   271→    lang,
   272→    state: dict,
   273→    file_contents: dict[str, str],
   274→    *,
   275→    allowed_files: set[str] | None = None,
   276→) -> dict:
   277→    testing: dict = {"total_files": len(file_contents)}
   278→    if not lang.dep_graph:
   279→        return testing
   280→
   281→    tc_findings = {
   282→        finding["file"]
   283→        for finding in state.get("findings", {}).values()
   284→        if finding.get("detector") == "test_coverage"
   285→        and finding.get("status") == "open"
   286→        and _in_allowed_files(finding.get("file", ""), allowed_files)
   287→    }
   288→    if not tc_findings:
   289→        return testing
   290→
   291→    critical_untested = []
   292→    for filepath in tc_findings:
   293→        entry = lang.dep_graph.get(resolve_path(filepath), {})
   294→        entry_importer_count = importer_count(entry)
   295→        if entry_importer_count >= 3:
   296→            critical_untested.append(
   297→                {"file": filepath, "importers": entry_importer_count}
   298→            )
   299→    testing["critical_untested"] = sorted(
   300→        critical_untested,
   301→        key=lambda item: -item["importers"],
   302→    )[:10]
   303→    return testing
   304→
   305→
   306→def _api_surface_context(lang, file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:
   307→    api_surface_fn = getattr(lang, "review_api_surface_fn", None)
   308→    if not callable(api_surface_fn):
   309→        return {}
   310→    computed = api_surface_fn(file_contents)
   311→    return computed if isinstance(computed, dict) else {}
   312→

   242→        if key in self.state.runtime_settings:

   244→        spec = self.config.setting_specs.get(key)
   245→        if spec:
   246→            return copy.deepcopy(spec.default)
   247→        return default
   248→
   249→    def runtime_option(self, key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
   250→        if key in self.state.runtime_options:
   251→            return self.state.runtime_options[key]
   252→        spec = self.config.runtime_option_specs.get(key)
   253→        if spec:

   255→        return default

   258→def _coerce_lang_override(field_name: str, value: object) -> object:
   259→    """Normalize override values to LangRuntimeState-compatible payloads."""
   260→    if field_name in _LANG_OVERRIDE_DICT_FIELDS:
   261→        return value or {}
   262→    if field_name in _LANG_OVERRIDE_LIST_FIELDS:
   263→        return value or []
   264→    if field_name in _LANG_OVERRIDE_INT_FIELDS:
   265→        return int(value or 0)
   266→    if field_name == "review_max_age_days":
   267→        if value is None:
   268→            return None
   269→        return int(value)
   270→    return value
   271→
   272→
   273→def _apply_lang_overrides(runtime: LangRun, overrides: LangRunOverrides) -> None:
   274→    """Apply override bundle to runtime state via one normalized loop."""
   275→    for field_name in _LANG_OVERRIDE_FIELDS:
   276→        value = getattr(overrides, field_name)
   277→        if value is _UNSET:
   278→            continue
   279→        coerced = _coerce_lang_override(field_name, value)
   280→        if field_name == "review_max_age_days" and coerced is None:
   281→            continue
   282→        setattr(runtime, field_name, coerced)
   283→
   284→
   285→def make_lang_run(
   286→    lang: LangConfig | LangRun,
   287→    overrides: LangRunOverrides | None = None,
   288→) -> LangRun:
   289→    """Build a fresh LangRun for a command invocation."""
   290→
   291→    if isinstance(lang, LangRun):
   292→        runtime = lang
   293→    else:
   294→        runtime = LangRun(config=lang)
   295→        runtime.state.runtime_settings = copy.deepcopy(
   296→            getattr(lang, "_default_runtime_settings", {})
   297→        )
   298→        runtime.state.runtime_options = copy.deepcopy(
   299→            getattr(lang, "_default_runtime_options", {})
   300→        )
   301→
   302→    resolved = overrides if overrides is not None else LangRunOverrides()
   303→    _apply_lang_overrides(runtime, resolved)
   304→    return runtime
   305→
   306→
   307→__all__ = [
   308→    "LangRuntimeContract",
   309→    "LangRun",
   310→    "LangRunOverrides",
   311→    "LangRuntimeState",
   312→    "make_lang_run",
   313→]

    26→def merge_potentials(potentials_by_lang: dict[str, dict[str, int]]) -> dict[str, int]:
    27→    """Sum potentials across languages per detector."""
    28→    merged: dict[str, int] = {}
    29→    for lang_potentials in potentials_by_lang.values():
    30→        for detector, count in lang_potentials.items():
    31→            merged[detector] = merged.get(detector, 0) + count
    32→    return merged

    35→def _iter_scoring_candidates(
    36→    detector: str,

    38→    excluded_zones: frozenset[str],

    41→    for finding in findings.values():

    43→            continue

    45→            continue
    46→        if finding.get("zone", "production") in excluded_zones:
    47→            continue
    48→        yield finding
    49→
    50→
    51→def _finding_weight(finding: Finding, *, use_loc_weight: bool) -> float:
    52→    """Compute the scoring weight for a single finding."""
    53→    if use_loc_weight:
    54→        return finding.get("detail", {}).get("loc_weight", 1.0)
    55→    return CONFIDENCE_WEIGHTS.get(finding.get("confidence", "medium"), 0.7)
    56→
    57→
    58→def _file_count_cap(findings_in_file: int) -> float:
    59→    """Tiered cap for non-LOC file-based detectors.
    60→
    61→    Keeps file-count denominator semantics while preserving concentration signal:
    62→    1-2 findings => _FILE_CAP_LOW, 3-5 => _FILE_CAP_MID, 6+ => _FILE_CAP_HIGH.
    63→    """
    64→    if findings_in_file >= _FILE_CAP_HIGH_THRESHOLD:
    65→        return _FILE_CAP_HIGH
    66→    if findings_in_file >= _FILE_CAP_MID_THRESHOLD:
    67→        return _FILE_CAP_MID
    68→    return _FILE_CAP_LOW
    69→
    70→
    71→@dataclass
    72→class _ModeAccum:
    73→    """Per-mode accumulator for file-based detector scoring."""
    74→
    75→    by_file: dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
    76→    by_file_count: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
    77→    file_cap: dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
    78→    holistic_sum: float = 0.0
    79→    issue_count: int = 0
    80→
    81→
    82→def _file_based_failures_by_mode(
    83→    detector: str,
    84→    findings: dict[str, Finding],
    85→    policy,
    86→) -> dict[ScoreMode, tuple[int, float]]:
    87→    """Accumulate weighted failures by score mode for file-based detectors."""
    88→    accum: dict[ScoreMode, _ModeAccum] = {mode: _ModeAccum() for mode in SCORING_MODES}
    89→
    90→    for finding in _iter_scoring_candidates(detector, findings, policy.excluded_zones):
    91→        status = finding.get("status", "open")
    92→        holistic = finding.get("file") == "." and finding.get("detail", {}).get(
    93→            "holistic"
    94→        )
    95→
    96→        for mode in SCORING_MODES:
    97→            if status not in FAILURE_STATUSES_BY_MODE[mode]:
    98→                continue
    99→
   100→            if holistic:
   101→                accum[mode].holistic_sum += (
   102→                    _finding_weight(finding, use_loc_weight=False) * HOLISTIC_MULTIPLIER
   103→                )
   104→                accum[mode].issue_count += 1
   105→                continue
   106→
   107→            weight = _finding_weight(finding, use_loc_weight=policy.use_loc_weight)
   108→            file_key = finding.get("file", "")
   109→            a = accum[mode]
   110→            a.by_file[file_key] = a.by_file.get(file_key, 0.0) + weight
   111→            a.by_file_count[file_key] = a.by_file_count.get(file_key, 0) + 1
   112→            if policy.use_loc_weight and file_key not in a.file_cap:
   113→                a.file_cap[file_key] = weight
   114→            a.issue_count += 1
   115→
   116→    out: dict[ScoreMode, tuple[int, float]] = {}
   117→    for mode in SCORING_MODES:
   118→        a = accum[mode]
   119→        if policy.use_loc_weight:
   120→            weighted = sum(
   121→                min(weighted_sum, a.file_cap.get(file_key, weighted_sum))
   122→                for file_key, weighted_sum in a.by_file.items()
   123→            )
   124→        else:
   125→            weighted = sum(
   126→                min(weighted_sum, _file_count_cap(a.by_file_count.get(file_key, 0)))
   127→                for file_key, weighted_sum in a.by_file.items()
   128→            )
   129→        out[mode] = (a.issue_count, weighted + a.holistic_sum)
   130→    return out
   131→
   132→
   133→def detector_stats_by_mode(
   134→    detector: str,
   135→    findings: dict[str, Finding],
   136→    potential: int,
   137→) -> dict[ScoreMode, tuple[float, int, float]]:
   138→    """Compute (pass_rate, issue_count, weighted_failures) for each score mode."""
   139→    if potential <= 0:
   140→        return {mode: (1.0, 0, 0.0) for mode in SCORING_MODES}
   141→
   142→    # Review and concern findings are scored via subjective assessments only —
   143→    # exclude them from the detection-side scoring pipeline so resolving these
   144→    # findings never changes the score directly.
   145→    if detector in ("review", "concerns"):
   146→        return {mode: (1.0, 0, 0.0) for mode in SCORING_MODES}
   147→
   148→    policy = detector_policy(detector)
   149→
   150→    if policy.file_based:
   151→        mode_failures = _file_based_failures_by_mode(detector, findings, policy)
   152→    else:
   153→        issue_count: dict[ScoreMode, int] = {mode: 0 for mode in SCORING_MODES}
   154→        weighted_failures: dict[ScoreMode, float] = {
   155→            mode: 0.0 for mode in SCORING_MODES
   156→        }
   157→
   158→        for finding in _iter_scoring_candidates(
   159→            detector, findings, policy.excluded_zones
   160→        ):
   161→            status = finding.get("status", "open")
   162→            weight = _finding_weight(finding, use_loc_weight=False)
   163→            for mode in SCORING_MODES:
   164→                if status not in FAILURE_STATUSES_BY_MODE[mode]:
   165→                    continue
   166→                issue_count[mode] += 1
   167→                weighted_failures[mode] += weight
   168→
   169→        mode_failures = {
   170→            mode: (issue_count[mode], weighted_failures[mode]) for mode in SCORING_MODES
   171→        }
   172→
   173→    out: dict[ScoreMode, tuple[float, int, float]] = {}
   174→    for mode in SCORING_MODES:
   175→        issues, weighted = mode_failures[mode]
   176→        pass_rate = max(0.0, (potential - weighted) / potential)
   177→        out[mode] = (pass_rate, issues, weighted)
   178→    return out
   179→
   180→
   181→def detector_pass_rate(
   182→    detector: str,
   183→    findings: dict[str, Finding],
   184→    potential: int,
   185→    *,
   186→    strict: bool = False,
   187→) -> tuple[float, int, float]:
   188→    """Pass rate for one detector.
   189→
   190→    Returns (pass_rate, issue_count, weighted_failures).
   191→    Zero potential -> (1.0, 0, 0.0).
   192→    """
   193→    mode: ScoreMode = "strict" if strict else "lenient"
   194→    return detector_stats_by_mode(detector, findings, potential)[mode]
   195→
   196→
   197→__all__ = [
   198→    "detector_pass_rate",
   199→    "detector_stats_by_mode",
   200→    "merge_potentials",
   201→]
   202→

1→"""Zone classification system — deterministic file intent classification.
     2→
     3→Classifies files into zones (production, test, config, generated, script, vendor)
     4→based on path patterns. Zone metadata flows through findings, scoring, and the LLM.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→from __future__ import annotations
     8→
     9→import logging
    10→import os
    11→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    12→from enum import Enum
    13→
    14→from desloppify.core.fallbacks import log_best_effort_failure
    15→from desloppify.engine.policy.zones_data import (
    16→    CONFIG_SKIP_DETECTORS,
    17→    SCRIPT_SKIP_DETECTORS,
    18→    SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
    19→    TEST_SKIP_DETECTORS,
    20→)
    21→
    22→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    23→
    24→
    25→class Zone(str, Enum):
    26→    """File intent zone — determines scoring and detection policy."""
    27→
    28→    PRODUCTION = "production"
    29→    TEST = "test"
    30→    CONFIG = "config"
    31→    GENERATED = "generated"
    32→    SCRIPT = "script"
    33→    VENDOR = "vendor"
    34→
    35→
    36→# Zones excluded from the health score
    37→EXCLUDED_ZONES = {Zone.TEST, Zone.CONFIG, Zone.GENERATED, Zone.VENDOR}
    38→
    39→# String values for quick lookup in scoring (findings store zone as string)
    40→EXCLUDED_ZONE_VALUES = {z.value for z in EXCLUDED_ZONES}
    41→
    42→
    43→@dataclass
    44→class ZoneRule:
    45→    """A classification rule: zone + list of path patterns.
    46→
    47→    Patterns are matched against relative file paths. First matching rule wins.
    48→    Pattern types (auto-detected from shape):
    49→      - "/dir/"   → substring match on full path (directory marker)
    50→      - ".ext"    → basename ends-with (suffix/extension, e.g. ".d.ts", ".test.")
    51→      - "prefix_" → basename starts-with (trailing underscore)
    52→      - "name.py" → basename exact match (has extension, no /)
    53→      - fallback  → substring on full path
    54→    """
    55→
    56→    zone: Zone
    57→    patterns: list[str]
    58→
    59→
    60→def _match_pattern(rel_path: str, pattern: str) -> bool:
    61→    """Match a zone pattern against a relative file path.
    62→
    63→    See ZoneRule docstring for pattern type conventions.
    64→    """
    65→    basename = os.path.basename(rel_path)
    66→
    67→    # Directory pattern: "/dir/" → substring on padded path
    68→    if pattern.startswith("/") and pattern.endswith("/"):
    69→        return pattern in ("/" + rel_path + "/")
    70→
    71→    # Suffix/extension pattern: starts with "." → contains on basename
    72→    if pattern.startswith("."):
    73→        return pattern in basename
    74→
    75→    # Prefix pattern: ends with "_" → basename starts-with
    76→    if pattern.endswith("_"):
    77→        return basename.startswith(pattern)
    78→
    79→    # Suffix pattern: starts with "_" → basename ends-with (_test.py, _pb2.py)
    80→    if pattern.startswith("_"):
    81→        return basename.endswith(pattern)
    82→
    83→    # Exact basename: has a proper file extension (1-5 chars after last dot),
    84→    # no "/" → exact basename match (config.py, setup.py, conftest.py)
    85→    if "/" not in pattern and "." in pattern:
    86→        ext = pattern.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
    87→        if ext and len(ext) <= 5 and ext.isalnum():
    88→            return basename == pattern
    89→
    90→    # Fallback: substring on full path (vite.config, tsconfig, eslint, etc.)
    91→    return pattern in rel_path
    92→
    93→
    94→# ── Common zone rules (shared across languages) ──────────
    95→
    96→COMMON_ZONE_RULES = [
    97→    ZoneRule(Zone.VENDOR, ["/vendor/", "/third_party/", "/vendored/"]),
    98→    ZoneRule(Zone.GENERATED, ["/generated/", "/__generated__/"]),
    99→    ZoneRule(Zone.TEST, ["/tests/", "/test/", "/fixtures/"]),
   100→    ZoneRule(Zone.SCRIPT, ["/scripts/", "/bin/"]),
   101→]
   102→
   103→
   104→def classify_file(
   105→    rel_path: str, rules: list[ZoneRule], overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None
   106→) -> Zone:
   107→    """Classify a file by its relative path. Overrides take priority."""
   108→    if overrides:
   109→        override = overrides.get(rel_path)
   110→        if override:
   111→            try:
   112→                return Zone(override)
   113→            except ValueError as exc:
   114→                log_best_effort_failure(
   115→                    logger, f"parse zone override for {rel_path}", exc
   116→                )
   117→    for rule in rules:
   118→        for pattern in rule.patterns:
   119→            if _match_pattern(rel_path, pattern):
   120→                return rule.zone
   121→    return Zone.PRODUCTION
   122→
   123→
   124→class FileZoneMap:
   125→    """Cached zone classification for a set of files.
   126→
   127→    Built once per scan from file list + zone rules.
   128→    """
   129→
   130→    def __init__(
   131→        self,
   132→        files: list[str],
   133→        rules: list[ZoneRule],
   134→        rel_fn=None,
   135→        overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None,
   136→    ):
   137→        """Build zone map.
   138→
   139→        Args:
   140→            files: List of file paths (absolute or relative).
   141→            rules: Ordered zone rules (first match wins).
   142→            rel_fn: Optional function to convert paths to relative.
   143→            overrides: Manual zone overrides {rel_path: zone_value}.
   144→        """
   145→        self._map: dict[str, Zone] = {}
   146→        self._overrides = overrides
   147→        for f in files:
   148→            rp = rel_fn(f) if rel_fn else f
   149→            self._map[f] = classify_file(rp, rules, overrides)
   150→
   151→    def get(self, path: str) -> Zone:
   152→        """Get zone for a file path. Returns PRODUCTION if not classified."""
   153→        return self._map.get(path, Zone.PRODUCTION)
   154→
   155→    def exclude(self, files: list[str], *zones: Zone) -> list[str]:
   156→        """Return files NOT in the given zones."""
   157→        zone_set = set(zones)
   158→        return [f for f in files if self._map.get(f, Zone.PRODUCTION) not in zone_set]
   159→
   160→    def include_only(self, files: list[str], *zones: Zone) -> list[str]:
   161→        """Return files that ARE in the given zones."""
   162→        zone_set = set(zones)
   163→        return [f for f in files if self._map.get(f, Zone.PRODUCTION) in zone_set]
   164→
   165→    def counts(self) -> dict[str, int]:
   166→        """Return file count per zone."""
   167→        counts: dict[str, int] = {}
   168→        for zone in self._map.values():
   169→            counts[zone.value] = counts.get(zone.value, 0) + 1
   170→        return counts
   171→
   172→    def production_count(self) -> int:
   173→        """Count files classified as production."""
   174→        return len(self._map) - self.non_production_count()
   175→
   176→    def non_production_count(self) -> int:
   177→        """Count files in excluded zones (test/config/generated/vendor)."""
   178→        return sum(1 for z in self._map.values() if z in EXCLUDED_ZONES)
   179→
   180→    def all_files(self) -> list[str]:
   181→        """Return all classified file paths."""
   182→        return list(self._map.keys())
   183→
   184→    def items(self) -> list[tuple[str, Zone]]:
   185→        """Return all (path, zone) pairs."""
   186→        return list(self._map.items())
   187→
   188→
   189→# ── Zone detection policies ────────────────────────────────
   190→
   191→
   192→@dataclass
   193→class ZonePolicy:
   194→    """Per-zone detection policy.
   195→
   196→    skip_detectors: detectors to skip entirely for this zone.
   197→    downgrade_detectors: detectors whose confidence is downgraded to "low".
   198→    exclude_from_score: whether findings in this zone are excluded from scoring.
   199→    """
   200→
   201→    skip_detectors: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
   202→    downgrade_detectors: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
   203→    exclude_from_score: bool = False
   204→
   205→
   206→ZONE_POLICIES: dict[Zone, ZonePolicy] = {
   207→    Zone.PRODUCTION: ZonePolicy(),
   208→    Zone.TEST: ZonePolicy(
   209→        skip_detectors=TEST_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   210→        downgrade_detectors={"smells", "structural"},
   211→        exclude_from_score=True,
   212→    ),
   213→    Zone.CONFIG: ZonePolicy(
   214→        skip_detectors=CONFIG_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   215→        exclude_from_score=True,
   216→    ),
   217→    Zone.GENERATED: ZonePolicy(
   218→        skip_detectors=SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
   219→        exclude_from_score=True,
   220→    ),
   221→    Zone.VENDOR: ZonePolicy(
   222→        skip_detectors=SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
   223→        exclude_from_score=True,
   224→    ),
   225→    Zone.SCRIPT: ZonePolicy(
   226→        skip_detectors=SCRIPT_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   227→        downgrade_detectors={"structural"},
   228→    ),
   229→}
   230→
   231→
   232→# ── Helpers for phase runners ─────────────────────────────
   233→
   234→
   235→def adjust_potential(zone_map, total: int) -> int:
   236→    """Subtract non-production files from a potential count.
   237→
   238→    Uses the zone map's own file list — no need to pass files separately.
   239→    No-op if zone_map is None.
   240→    """
   241→    if zone_map is None:
   242→        return total
   243→    return max(total - zone_map.non_production_count(), 0)
   244→
   245→
   246→def should_skip_finding(zone_map, filepath: str, detector: str) -> bool:
   247→    """Check if a finding should be skipped based on zone policy.
   248→
   249→    Returns True if the file's zone policy says to skip this detector.
   250→    """
   251→    if zone_map is None:
   252→        return False
   253→    zone = zone_map.get(filepath)
   254→    policy = ZONE_POLICIES.get(zone)
   255→    return policy is not None and detector in policy.skip_detectors
   256→
   257→
   258→def filter_entries(
   259→    zone_map, entries: list[dict], detector: str, file_key: str = "file"
   260→) -> list[dict]:
   261→    """Filter detector entries by zone policy. No-op if zone_map is None.
   262→
   263→    If file_key points to a list (e.g. cycle entries with "files"), checks
   264→    the first element.

   266→    if zone_map is None:

   273→    return [

1→"""Runtime state model for exclusions and in-memory caches."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from contextlib import contextmanager
     6→from contextvars import ContextVar
     7→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
     8→from pathlib import Path
     9→
    10→
    11→class FileTextCache:
    12→    """Optional read-through file-text cache used by scan/review passes."""
    13→
    14→    def __init__(self) -> None:
    15→        self._enabled = False
    16→        self._values: dict[str, str | None] = {}
    17→
    18→    def enable(self) -> None:
    19→        self._enabled = True
    20→        self._values.clear()
    21→
    22→    def disable(self) -> None:
    23→        self._enabled = False
    24→        self._values.clear()
    25→
    26→    def read(self, filepath: str) -> str | None:
    27→        if self._enabled and filepath in self._values:
    28→            return self._values[filepath]
    29→
    30→        try:
    31→            content = Path(filepath).read_text(errors="replace")
    32→        except OSError:
    33→            content = None
    34→        if self._enabled:
    35→            self._values[filepath] = content
    36→        return content
    37→
    38→
    39→class SourceFileCache:
    40→    """Small FIFO cache for source-file discovery results."""
    41→
    42→    def __init__(self, *, max_entries: int) -> None:
    43→        self.max_entries = max_entries
    44→        self.values: dict[tuple, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
    45→
    46→    def get(self, key: tuple) -> tuple[str, ...] | None:
    47→        return self.values.get(key)
    48→
    49→    def put(self, key: tuple, value: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
    50→        if len(self.values) >= self.max_entries:
    51→            self.values.pop(next(iter(self.values)))
    52→        self.values[key] = value
    53→
    54→    def clear(self) -> None:
    55→        self.values.clear()
    56→
    57→
    58→@dataclass
    59→class RuntimeContext:
    60→    """Mutable runtime container for exclusion and cache state."""
    61→
    62→    exclusions: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    63→    project_root: Path | None = None
    64→    query_file: Path | None = None
    65→    file_text_cache: FileTextCache = field(default_factory=FileTextCache)
    66→    cache_enabled: bool = False
    67→    source_file_cache: SourceFileCache = field(
    68→        default_factory=lambda: SourceFileCache(max_entries=16)
    69→    )
    70→
    71→
    72→_PROCESS_RUNTIME_CONTEXT = RuntimeContext()
    73→_RUNTIME_CONTEXT: ContextVar[RuntimeContext | None] = ContextVar(
    74→    "desloppify_runtime_context",
    75→    default=None,
    76→)
    77→
    78→
    79→def make_runtime_context(*, source_file_cache_max_entries: int = 16) -> RuntimeContext:
    80→    """Create an isolated runtime context."""
    81→    return RuntimeContext(
    82→        source_file_cache=SourceFileCache(max_entries=source_file_cache_max_entries)
    83→    )
    84→
    85→
    86→def current_runtime_context() -> RuntimeContext:
    87→    """Return the active runtime context (or process fallback)."""
    88→    runtime = _RUNTIME_CONTEXT.get()
    89→    if runtime is not None:
    90→        return runtime
    91→    return _PROCESS_RUNTIME_CONTEXT
    92→
    93→
    94→@contextmanager
    95→def runtime_scope(runtime: RuntimeContext | None = None):
    96→    """Run code with an isolated runtime context."""
    97→    active = runtime or make_runtime_context()
    98→    [REDACTED](active)
    99→    try:
   100→        yield active
   101→    finally:
   102→        _RUNTIME_CONTEXT.reset(token)
   103→

     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import copy
     6→

     8→    "coerce_assessment_score",
     9→    "match_findings",
    10→    "resolve_findings",
    11→]
    12→
    13→from desloppify.core._internal.text_utils import is_numeric
    14→from desloppify.engine._state.filtering import _matches_pattern
    15→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import (
    16→    StateModel,
    17→    ensure_state_defaults,
    18→    utc_now,
    19→    validate_state_invariants,
    20→)
    21→from desloppify.engine._state.scoring import _recompute_stats
    22→
    23→
    24→def coerce_assessment_score(value: object) -> float | None:
    25→    """Normalize a subjective assessment score payload to a 0-100 float.
    26→
    27→    Returns ``None`` when the value cannot be interpreted as a numeric score
    28→    (e.g. bools, non-numeric strings, missing keys).
    29→    """
    30→    if is_numeric(value):
    31→        return round(max(0.0, min(100.0, float(value))), 1)
    32→    if isinstance(value, dict):
    33→        raw = value.get("score")
    34→        if not is_numeric(raw):
    35→            return None
    36→        return round(max(0.0, min(100.0, float(raw))), 1)
    37→    return None
    38→
    39→
    40→def _mark_stale_assessments_on_review_resolve(
    41→    state: StateModel,
    42→    *,
    43→    status: str,
    44→    resolved_findings: list[dict],
    45→    now: str,
    46→) -> None:
    47→    """Mark subjective assessments as stale when review findings are resolved.
    48→
    49→    The assessment score is preserved (not zeroed) — only a fresh review import
    50→    should change dimension scores.  The stale marker tells the UI to prompt
    51→    for a re-review.
    52→    """
    53→    assessments = state.get("subjective_assessments")
    54→    if not isinstance(assessments, dict) or not assessments:
    55→        return
    56→
    57→    touched_dimensions: set[str] = set()
    58→    for finding in resolved_findings:
    59→        if finding.get("detector") != "review":
    60→            continue
    61→        dimension = str(finding.get("detail", {}).get("dimension", "")).strip()
    62→        if dimension:
    63→            touched_dimensions.add(dimension)
    64→
    65→    for dimension in sorted(touched_dimensions):
    66→        if dimension not in assessments:
    67→            continue
    68→
    69→        payload = assessments.get(dimension)
    70→        if isinstance(payload, dict):
    71→            payload["needs_review_refresh"] = True
    72→            payload["refresh_reason"] = f"review_finding_{status}"
    73→            payload["stale_since"] = now
    74→        else:
    75→            assessments[dimension] = {
    76→                "score": coerce_assessment_score(payload) or 0.0,
    77→                "needs_review_refresh": True,
    78→                "refresh_reason": f"review_finding_{status}",
    79→                "stale_since": now,
    80→            }
    81→
    82→
    83→def match_findings(
    84→    state: StateModel, pattern: str, status_filter: str = "open"
    85→) -> list[dict]:
    86→    """Return findings matching *pattern* with the given status."""
    87→    ensure_state_defaults(state)
    88→    return [
    89→        finding
    90→        for finding_id, finding in state["findings"].items()
    91→        if not finding.get("suppressed")
    92→        if (status_filter == "all" or finding["status"] == status_filter)
    93→        and _matches_pattern(finding_id, finding, pattern)
    94→    ]
    95→
    96→
    97→def resolve_findings(
    98→    state: StateModel,
    99→    pattern: str,
   100→    status: str,
   101→    note: str | None = None,
   102→    attestation: str | None = None,
   103→) -> list[str]:
   104→    """Set finding status for matches and return affected finding IDs."""
   105→    ensure_state_defaults(state)
   106→    now = utc_now()
   107→    resolved: list[str] = []
   108→    resolved_findings: list[dict] = []
   109→    status_filter = "all" if status == "open" else "open"
   110→    for finding in match_findings(state, pattern, status_filter=status_filter):
   111→        previous_status = str(finding.get("status", "open")).strip() or "open"
   112→        if status == "open" and previous_status == "open":
   113→            continue
   114→
   115→        extra_updates: dict[str, object] = {}
   116→        if status == "wontfix":
   117→            snapshot_scan_count = int(state.get("scan_count", 0) or 0)
   118→            extra_updates["wontfix_scan_count"] = snapshot_scan_count
   119→            extra_updates["wontfix_snapshot"] = {
   120→                "captured_at": now,
   121→                "scan_count": snapshot_scan_count,
   122→                "tier": finding.get("tier"),
   123→                "confidence": finding.get("confidence"),
   124→                "detail": copy.deepcopy(finding.get("detail", {})),
   125→            }
   126→        if status == "open":
   127→            finding["reopen_count"] = int(finding.get("reopen_count", 0) or 0) + 1
   128→            finding.pop("wontfix_scan_count", None)
   129→            finding.pop("wontfix_snapshot", None)
   130→            previous_note = finding.get("note")
   131→            next_note = note if note is not None else previous_note
   132→            extra_updates["resolved_at"] = None
   133→            extra_updates["note"] = next_note
   134→            reopen_attestation = {
   135→                "kind": "manual_reopen",
   136→                "text": attestation or note,
   137→                "attested_at": now,
   138→                "scan_verified": False,
   139→            }
   140→            reopen_attestation["previous_status"] = previous_status
   141→            extra_updates["resolution_attestation"] = reopen_attestation
   142→
   143→        updates: dict[str, object] = {
   144→            "status": status,
   145→            "note": note,
   146→            "resolved_at": now,
   147→            "suppressed": False,
   148→            "suppressed_at": None,
   149→            "suppression_pattern": None,
   150→            "resolution_attestation": {
   151→                "kind": "manual",
   152→                "text": attestation,
   153→                "attested_at": now,
   154→                "scan_verified": False,
   155→            },
   156→        }
   157→        updates.update(extra_updates)
   158→        finding.update(updates)
   159→        resolved.append(finding["id"])
   160→        resolved_findings.append(finding)
   161→
   162→    _mark_stale_assessments_on_review_resolve(
   163→        state,
   164→        status=status,
   165→        resolved_findings=resolved_findings,
   166→        now=now,
   167→    )
   168→
   169→    _recompute_stats(state, scan_path=state.get("scan_path"))
   170→    validate_state_invariants(state)
   171→    return resolved
   172→

    23→def write_show_output_file(output_file: str, payload: dict, surfaced_count: int) -> bool:

    27→        print(colorize(f"Wrote {surfaced_count} findings to {output_file}", "green"))

    35→def group_matches_by_file(matches: list[dict]) -> list[tuple[str, list]]:
    36→    """Group findings by file and sort by descending count."""
    37→    by_file: dict[str, list] = defaultdict(list)
    38→    for finding in matches:
    39→        by_file[finding["file"]].append(finding)
    40→    return sorted(by_file.items(), key=lambda item: -len(item[1]))

1→"""Language plugin discovery and import error surfacing."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import importlib
     6→import importlib.util
     7→import logging
     8→from pathlib import Path
     9→
    10→from . import registry_state
    11→
    12→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    13→
    14→# Broader than PARSE_INIT_ERRORS: plugin imports may also raise SyntaxError/TypeError.
    15→_PLUGIN_IMPORT_ERRORS: tuple[type[Exception], ...] = (
    16→    ImportError, SyntaxError, ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError, OSError,
    17→)
    18→
    19→
    20→def raise_load_errors() -> None:
    21→    errors = registry_state.get_load_errors()
    22→    if not errors:
    23→        return
    24→    summaries: list[str] = []
    25→    for module_name, ex in sorted(errors.items()):
    26→        ex_type = type(ex).__name__
    27→        logger.warning(
    28→            "Language plugin %s failed to load: %s: %s",
    29→            module_name,
    30→            ex_type,
    31→            ex,
    32→        )
    33→        summaries.append(f"{module_name}: {ex_type}: {ex}")
    34→    raise ImportError("; ".join(summaries))
    35→
    36→
    37→def _report_load_errors_for_load_all() -> None:
    38→    """Emit warning diagnostics for plugin failures without aborting discovery."""
    39→    try:
    40→        raise_load_errors()
    41→    except ImportError:
    42→        # load_all historically logs plugin failures and continues so command
    43→        # startup can proceed with the languages that did load successfully.
    44→        return
    45→
    46→
    47→def load_all() -> None:
    48→    """Import all language modules to trigger registration."""
    49→    if registry_state.was_load_attempted():
    50→        _report_load_errors_for_load_all()
    51→        return
    52→
    53→    lang_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    54→    if lang_dir.name == "_framework":
    55→        lang_dir = lang_dir.parent
    56→    base_package = __package__.rsplit(".", 1)[0]
    57→    failures: dict[str, BaseException] = {}
    58→
    59→    # Discover single-file plugins by naming convention (e.g. plugin_rust.py).
    60→    for f in sorted(lang_dir.glob("plugin_*.py")):
    61→        module_name = f".{f.stem}"
    62→        try:
    63→            importlib.import_module(module_name, base_package)
    64→        except _PLUGIN_IMPORT_ERRORS as ex:
    65→            logger.debug("Language plugin import failed for %s: %s", module_name, ex)
    66→            failures[module_name] = ex
    67→
    68→    # Discover packages (e.g. lang/typescript/)
    69→    for d in sorted(lang_dir.iterdir()):
    70→        if (
    71→            d.is_dir()
    72→            and (d / "__init__.py").exists()
    73→            and not d.name.startswith("_")
    74→        ):
    75→            module_name = f".{d.name}"
    76→            try:
    77→                importlib.import_module(module_name, base_package)
    78→            except _PLUGIN_IMPORT_ERRORS as ex:
    79→                logger.debug(
    80→                    "Language package import failed for %s: %s", module_name, ex
    81→                )
    82→                failures[module_name] = ex
    83→
    84→    # Discover user plugins from <active-project-root>/.desloppify/plugins/*.py
    85→    try:
    86→        from desloppify.core._internal.text_utils import get_project_root
    87→
    88→        user_plugin_dir = get_project_root() / ".desloppify" / "plugins"
    89→        if user_plugin_dir.is_dir():
    90→            for f in sorted(user_plugin_dir.glob("*.py")):
    91→                spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
    92→                    f"desloppify_user_plugin_{f.stem}", f
    93→                )
    94→                if spec and spec.loader:
    95→                    try:
    96→                        mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    97→                        spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    98→                    except _PLUGIN_IMPORT_ERRORS as ex:
    99→                        logger.debug(
   100→                            "User plugin import failed for %s: %s", f.name, ex
   101→                        )
   102→                        failures[f"user:{f.name}"] = ex
   103→    except (OSError, ImportError) as exc:
   104→        logger.debug("User plugin discovery skipped: %s", exc)
   105→
   106→    registry_state.set_load_attempted(True)
   107→    registry_state.set_load_errors(failures)

1→"""Load and validate review dimension payloads from JSON data files."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import copy
     6→import json
     7→from functools import lru_cache
     8→from pathlib import Path
     9→
    10→from desloppify.intelligence.review.feedback_contract import ensure_prompt_contract
    11→from desloppify.intelligence.review.dimensions.validation import (
    12→    parse_dimensions_payload,
    13→)
    14→
    15→_LANG_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "languages"
    16→_LANG_DATA_SUBDIR = "review_data"
    17→_DATA_DIR = _LANG_DIR / "_framework" / _LANG_DATA_SUBDIR
    18→
    19→# Canonical filename for the unified dimensions payload.
    20→_DIMENSIONS_FILE = "dimensions.json"
    21→
    22→
    23→def _load_json_payload_from_path(path: Path) -> dict:
    24→    """Load a JSON payload from *path* and return a dict."""
    25→    try:
    26→        raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    27→    except OSError as exc:
    28→        raise RuntimeError(f"Unable to read dimensions payload: {path}") from exc
    29→
    30→    try:
    31→        payload = json.loads(raw)
    32→    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
    33→        raise ValueError(f"Invalid JSON in dimensions payload: {path}") from exc
    34→
    35→    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
    36→        raise ValueError(f"Dimensions payload must be a JSON object: {path}")
    37→    return payload
    38→
    39→
    40→def _lang_payload_path(lang_name: str, filename: str) -> Path:
    41→    """Resolve the per-language review payload path."""
    42→    return _LANG_DIR / lang_name / _LANG_DATA_SUBDIR / filename
    43→
    44→
    45→def _override_filename(filename: str) -> str:
    46→    """Convert ``foo.json`` to ``foo.override.json``."""
    47→    if not filename.endswith(".json"):
    48→        return f"{filename}.override.json"
    49→    return f"{filename[:-5]}.override.json"
    50→
    51→
    52→def _load_json_payload(filename: str) -> dict:
    53→    """Load a JSON payload from the shared language review-data directory."""
    54→    return _load_json_payload_from_path(_DATA_DIR / filename)
    55→
    56→
    57→def _validate_optional_string_list(value: object, *, context: str) -> list[str]:
    58→    """Validate an optional list of strings (empty allowed)."""
    59→    if value is None:
    60→        return []
    61→    if not isinstance(value, list):
    62→        raise ValueError(f"{context} must be a list of strings")
    63→    out: list[str] = []
    64→    for idx, item in enumerate(value):
    65→        if not isinstance(item, str) or not item.strip():
    66→            raise ValueError(f"{context}[{idx}] must be a non-empty string")
    67→        out.append(item)
    68→    return out
    69→
    70→
    71→def _apply_dimensions_override(
    72→    base_payload: dict,
    73→    override_payload: dict,
    74→    *,
    75→    dims_key: str,
    76→    context: str,
    77→) -> dict:
    78→    """Apply a language override payload to a base dimensions payload."""
    79→    if not isinstance(override_payload, dict):
    80→        raise ValueError(f"{context} must be a JSON object")
    81→
    82→    allowed = {
    83→        dims_key,
    84→        f"{dims_key}_append",
    85→        f"{dims_key}_remove",
    86→        "dimension_prompts",
    87→        "dimension_prompts_remove",
    88→        "system_prompt",
    89→        "system_prompt_append",
    90→    }
    91→    actual = set(override_payload)
    92→    extra = sorted(actual - allowed)
    93→    if extra:
    94→        raise ValueError(f"{context} has unsupported keys: {extra}")
    95→
    96→    out = copy.deepcopy(base_payload)
    97→
    98→    if dims_key in override_payload:
    99→        out[dims_key] = override_payload[dims_key]
   100→
   101→    dims = list(out.get(dims_key, []))
   102→    for dim in _validate_optional_string_list(
   103→        override_payload.get(f"{dims_key}_append"),
   104→        context=f"{context}.{dims_key}_append",
   105→    ):
   106→        if dim not in dims:
   107→            dims.append(dim)
   108→
   109→    remove_dims = set(
   110→        _validate_optional_string_list(
   111→            override_payload.get(f"{dims_key}_remove"),
   112→            context=f"{context}.{dims_key}_remove",
   113→        )
   114→    )
   115→    if remove_dims:
   116→        dims = [dim for dim in dims if dim not in remove_dims]
   117→    out[dims_key] = dims
   118→
   119→    if "dimension_prompts" in override_payload:
   120→        prompt_overrides = override_payload["dimension_prompts"]
   121→        if not isinstance(prompt_overrides, dict):
   122→            raise ValueError(f"{context}.dimension_prompts must be an object")
   123→        prompts = dict(out.get("dimension_prompts", {}))
   124→        for dim_name, prompt in prompt_overrides.items():
   125→            prompts[dim_name] = prompt
   126→        out["dimension_prompts"] = prompts
   127→
   128→    remove_prompts = _validate_optional_string_list(
   129→        override_payload.get("dimension_prompts_remove"),
   130→        context=f"{context}.dimension_prompts_remove",
   131→    )
   132→    if remove_prompts:
   133→        prompts = dict(out.get("dimension_prompts", {}))
   134→        for dim_name in remove_prompts:
   135→            prompts.pop(dim_name, None)
   136→        out["dimension_prompts"] = prompts
   137→
   138→    if "system_prompt" in override_payload:
   139→        out["system_prompt"] = override_payload["system_prompt"]
   140→    if "system_prompt_append" in override_payload:
   141→        suffix = override_payload["system_prompt_append"]
   142→        if not isinstance(suffix, str):
   143→            raise ValueError(f"{context}.system_prompt_append must be a string")
   144→        current = out.get("system_prompt", "")
   145→        sep = "\n\n" if current and suffix else ""
   146→        out["system_prompt"] = f"{current}{sep}{suffix}"
   147→
   148→    return out
   149→
   150→
   151→def _load_payload_for_lang(
   152→    lang_name: str,
   153→    filename: str,
   154→    *,
   155→    dims_key: str,
   156→) -> tuple[dict, str]:
   157→    """Load payload for a language using shared-base + optional language overlay.
   158→
   159→    Resolution order:
   160→    1) Start from shared base payload in ``lang/framework/review_data``.
   161→    2) If language override payload exists, patch the selected base.
   162→    """
   163→    base_payload = _load_json_payload(filename)
   164→    context = filename
   165→
   166→    lang_override_path = _lang_payload_path(lang_name, _override_filename(filename))
   167→    if lang_override_path.is_file():
   168→        override_payload = _load_json_payload_from_path(lang_override_path)
   169→        base_payload = _apply_dimensions_override(
   170→            base_payload,
   171→            override_payload,
   172→            dims_key=dims_key,
   173→            context=str(lang_override_path),
   174→        )
   175→        context = f"{context} + {lang_override_path}"
   176→
   177→    return base_payload, context
   178→
   179→
   180→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   181→# Canonical loaders — use these for new code.
   182→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   183→
   184→
   185→@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
   186→def load_dimensions() -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]:
   187→    """Load and validate the unified review dimension definitions."""
   188→    payload = _load_json_payload(_DIMENSIONS_FILE)
   189→    dims, prompts, system_prompt = parse_dimensions_payload(
   190→        payload, context_prefix=_DIMENSIONS_FILE
   191→    )
   192→    return dims, prompts, ensure_prompt_contract(system_prompt)
   193→
   194→
   195→@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
   196→def load_dimensions_for_lang(
   197→    lang_name: str,
   198→) -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]:
   199→    """Load unified review dimensions for a language (with lang override applied)."""

   201→        lang_name,
   202→        _DIMENSIONS_FILE,
   203→        [REDACTED],
   204→    )
   205→    dims, prompts, system_prompt = parse_dimensions_payload(
   206→        payload, context_prefix=context
   207→    )
   208→    return dims, prompts, ensure_prompt_contract(system_prompt)

1→"""State filtering, ignore rules, and finding pattern matching."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import fnmatch
     6→
     7→__all__ = [
     8→    "finding_in_scan_scope",
     9→    "open_scope_breakdown",
    10→    "path_scoped_findings",
    11→    "is_ignored",
    12→    "matched_ignore_pattern",
    13→    "remove_ignored_findings",
    14→    "add_ignore",
    15→    "make_finding",
    16→]
    17→
    18→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import (
    19→    Finding,
    20→    StateModel,
    21→    ensure_state_defaults,
    22→    utc_now,
    23→    validate_state_invariants,
    24→)
    25→from desloppify.core.discovery_api import rel
    26→
    27→
    28→def path_scoped_findings(
    29→    findings: dict[str, Finding],
    30→    scan_path: str | None,
    31→) -> dict[str, Finding]:
    32→    """Filter findings to those within the given scan path."""
    33→    return {
    34→        finding_id: finding
    35→        for finding_id, finding in findings.items()
    36→        if finding_in_scan_scope(str(finding.get("file", "")), scan_path)
    37→    }
    38→
    39→
    40→def finding_in_scan_scope(file_path: str, scan_path: str | None) -> bool:
    41→    """Return True when a file path belongs to the active scan scope."""
    42→    if not scan_path or scan_path == ".":
    43→        return True
    44→    prefix = scan_path.rstrip("/") + "/"
    45→    return (
    46→        file_path.startswith(prefix)
    47→        or file_path == scan_path
    48→        or file_path == "."
    49→    )
    50→
    51→
    52→def open_scope_breakdown(
    53→    findings: dict[str, Finding],
    54→    scan_path: str | None,
    55→    *,
    56→    detector: str | None = None,
    57→) -> dict[str, int]:
    58→    """Return open-finding counts split by in-scope vs out-of-scope carryover."""
    59→    in_scope = 0
    60→    out_of_scope = 0
    61→
    62→    for finding in findings.values():
    63→        if finding.get("suppressed"):
    64→            continue
    65→        if finding.get("status") != "open":
    66→            continue
    67→        if detector is not None and finding.get("detector") != detector:
    68→            continue
    69→        file_path = str(finding.get("file", ""))
    70→        if finding_in_scan_scope(file_path, scan_path):
    71→            in_scope += 1
    72→        else:
    73→            out_of_scope += 1
    74→
    75→    return {
    76→        "in_scope": in_scope,
    77→        "out_of_scope": out_of_scope,
    78→        "global": in_scope + out_of_scope,
    79→    }
    80→
    81→
    82→def is_ignored(finding_id: str, file: str, ignore_patterns: list[str]) -> bool:
    83→    """Check if a finding matches any ignore pattern (glob, ID prefix, or file path)."""
    84→    return matched_ignore_pattern(finding_id, file, ignore_patterns) is not None
    85→
    86→
    87→def matched_ignore_pattern(
    88→    finding_id: str, file: str, ignore_patterns: list[str]
    89→) -> str | None:
    90→    """Return the ignore pattern that matched, if any."""
    91→    for pattern in ignore_patterns:
    92→        if "*" in pattern:
    93→            target = finding_id if "::" in pattern else file
    94→            if fnmatch.fnmatch(target, pattern):
    95→                return pattern
    96→            continue
    97→
    98→        if "::" in pattern:
    99→            if finding_id.startswith(pattern):
   100→                return pattern
   101→            continue
   102→
   103→        if file == pattern or file == rel(pattern):
   104→            return pattern
   105→
   106→    return None
   107→
   108→
   109→def remove_ignored_findings(state: StateModel, pattern: str) -> int:
   110→    """Suppress findings matching an ignore pattern. Returns count affected."""
   111→    ensure_state_defaults(state)
   112→    matched_ids = [
   113→        finding_id
   114→        for finding_id, finding in state["findings"].items()
   115→        if is_ignored(finding_id, finding["file"], [pattern])
   116→    ]
   117→    now = utc_now()
   118→    for finding_id in matched_ids:
   119→        finding = state["findings"][finding_id]
   120→        finding["suppressed"] = True
   121→        finding["suppressed_at"] = now
   122→        finding["suppression_pattern"] = pattern
   123→    # Deferred import to avoid circular dependency with engine._state.scoring
   124→    from desloppify.engine._state.scoring import _recompute_stats
   125→
   126→    _recompute_stats(state, scan_path=state.get("scan_path"))
   127→    validate_state_invariants(state)
   128→    return len(matched_ids)
   129→
   130→
   131→def add_ignore(state: StateModel, pattern: str) -> int:
   132→    """Add an ignore pattern and remove existing matching findings."""
   133→    ensure_state_defaults(state)
   134→    config = state.setdefault("config", {})
   135→    ignores = config.setdefault("ignore", [])
   136→    if pattern not in ignores:
   137→        ignores.append(pattern)
   138→    return remove_ignored_findings(state, pattern)
   139→
   140→
   141→def make_finding(
   142→    detector: str,
   143→    file: str,
   144→    name: str,
   145→    *,
   146→    tier: int,
   147→    confidence: str,
   148→    summary: str,
   149→    detail: dict | None = None,
   150→) -> Finding:
   151→    """Create a normalized finding dict with a stable ID."""
   152→    rfile = rel(file)
   153→    finding_id = f"{detector}::{rfile}::{name}" if name else f"{detector}::{rfile}"
   154→    now = utc_now()
   155→    return {
   156→        "id": finding_id,
   157→        "detector": detector,
   158→        "file": rfile,
   159→        "tier": tier,
   160→        "confidence": confidence,
   161→        "summary": summary,
   162→        "detail": detail or {},
   163→        "status": "open",
   164→        "note": None,
   165→        "first_seen": now,
   166→        "last_seen": now,
   167→        "resolved_at": None,
   168→        "reopen_count": 0,
   169→    }
   170→
   171→
   172→def _matches_pattern(finding_id: str, finding: dict[str, str], pattern: str) -> bool:
   173→    """Check if a finding matches by ID, glob, prefix, detector, or path."""
   174→    return (
   175→        finding_id == pattern
   176→        or ("*" in pattern and fnmatch.fnmatch(finding_id, pattern))
   177→        or ("::" in pattern and finding_id.startswith(pattern))
   178→        or (
   179→            finding.get("detector") == pattern
   180→            or finding["file"] == pattern
   181→            or finding["file"].startswith(pattern.rstrip("/") + "/")
   182→        )
   183→    )
   184→

    45→class WorkQueueResult(TypedDict):

    57→
    58→def _apply_plan_order(
    59→    items: list[dict],
    60→    plan: dict,
    61→    *,
    62→    include_skipped: bool = False,
    63→    cluster: str | None = None,
    64→) -> list[dict]:
    65→    """Reorder items according to the living plan.
    66→
    67→    1. Items in ``queue_order`` appear first, in that order.
    68→    2. Remaining items keep their mechanical sort.
