    72→    queue_order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
    73→    skipped_map: dict = plan.get("skipped", {})
    74→    skipped_ids: set[str] = set(skipped_map.keys())
    75→    overrides: dict = plan.get("overrides", {})
    76→    clusters: dict = plan.get("clusters", {})
    77→    active_cluster = plan.get("active_cluster")
    78→
    79→    # Build lookup
    80→    by_id: dict[str, dict] = {}
    81→    for item in items:
    82→        by_id[item["id"]] = item
    83→
    84→    # Annotate items with plan metadata
    85→    for item_id, item in by_id.items():
    86→        override = overrides.get(item_id, {})
    87→        if override.get("description"):
    88→            item["plan_description"] = override["description"]
    89→        if override.get("note"):
    90→            item["plan_note"] = override["note"]
    91→        if override.get("cluster"):
    92→            cluster_name = override["cluster"]
    93→            cluster_data = clusters.get(cluster_name, {})
    94→            item["plan_cluster"] = {
    95→                "name": cluster_name,
    96→                "description": cluster_data.get("description"),
    97→                "total_items": len(cluster_data.get("finding_ids", [])),
    98→                "sibling_ids": cluster_data.get("finding_ids", []),
    99→            }
   100→
   101→    # Split into ordered, remaining, skipped
   102→    ordered: list[dict] = []
   103→    ordered_ids: set[str] = set()
   104→    for fid in queue_order:
   105→        if fid in by_id and fid not in skipped_ids:
   106→            ordered.append(by_id[fid])
   107→            ordered_ids.add(fid)
   108→
   109→    skipped_items: list[dict] = []
   110→    remaining: list[dict] = []
   111→    for item in items:
   112→        item_id = item["id"]
   113→        if item_id in ordered_ids:
   114→            continue
   115→        if item_id in skipped_ids:
   116→            skipped_items.append(item)
   117→        else:
   118→            remaining.append(item)
   119→
   120→    # Assign queue positions
   121→    result = ordered + remaining
   122→    if include_skipped:
   123→        result = result + skipped_items
   124→
   125→    for pos, item in enumerate(result):
   126→        item["queue_position"] = pos + 1
   127→        if item["id"] in skipped_ids:
   128→            item["plan_skipped"] = True
   129→            skip_entry = skipped_map.get(item["id"])
   130→            if skip_entry:
   131→                item["plan_skip_kind"] = skip_entry.get("kind", "temporary")
   132→                skip_reason = skip_entry.get("reason")
   133→                if skip_reason:
   134→                    item["plan_skip_reason"] = skip_reason
   135→
   136→    # Filter to cluster if requested
   137→    effective_cluster = cluster or active_cluster
   138→    if effective_cluster:
   139→        cluster_data = clusters.get(effective_cluster, {})
   140→        cluster_member_ids = set(cluster_data.get("finding_ids", []))
   141→        if cluster_member_ids:
   142→            result = [item for item in result if item["id"] in cluster_member_ids]
   143→
   144→    return result
   145→
   146→
   147→def _item_matches_tier(item: dict, tier: int) -> bool:
   148→    """Check if an item (or any of its members for clusters) matches a tier."""
   149→    if item.get("kind") == "cluster":
   150→        return any(
   151→            int(m.get("effective_tier", m.get("tier", 3))) == tier
   152→            for m in item.get("members", [])
   153→        )
   154→    return int(item.get("effective_tier", item.get("tier", 3))) == tier
   155→
   156→
   157→def _action_type_for_detector(detector: str) -> str:
   158→    """Look up the action_type for a detector from the registry."""
   159→    try:
   160→        from desloppify.core.registry import DETECTORS
   161→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   162→        if meta:
   163→            return meta.action_type
   164→    except ImportError:
   165→        pass
   166→    return "manual_fix"
   167→
   168→
   169→_ACTION_TYPE_PRIORITY = {"auto_fix": 0, "reorganize": 1, "refactor": 2, "manual_fix": 3}
   170→
   171→
   172→def _collapse_clusters(items: list[dict], plan: dict) -> list[dict]:
   173→    """Replace cluster member items with single cluster meta-items."""
   174→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   175→    if not clusters:
   176→        return items
   177→
   178→    # Build mapping: finding_id → auto-cluster name
   179→    fid_to_cluster: dict[str, str] = {}
   180→    for name, cluster in clusters.items():
   181→        if not cluster.get("auto"):
   182→            continue
   183→        for fid in cluster.get("finding_ids", []):
   184→            fid_to_cluster[fid] = name
   185→
   186→    if not fid_to_cluster:
   187→        return items
   188→
   189→    # Collect members for each cluster, preserving order
   190→    cluster_members: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
   191→    non_cluster_items: list[dict] = []
   192→
   193→    for item in items:
   194→        cname = fid_to_cluster.get(item.get("id", ""))
   195→        if cname:
   196→            cluster_members.setdefault(cname, []).append(item)
   197→        else:
   198→            non_cluster_items.append(item)
   199→
   200→    # Build cluster meta-items
   201→    result: list[dict] = list(non_cluster_items)
   202→    for cname, members in cluster_members.items():
   203→        # Don't collapse singletons — show them as individual findings
   204→        if len(members) < 2:
   205→            result.extend(members)
   206→            continue
   207→        cluster_data = clusters.get(cname, {})
   208→        detector = members[0].get("detector", "") if members else ""
   209→        action = cluster_data.get("action") or ""
   210→        # Derive action_type from the actual cluster action, not just the detector
   211→        if "desloppify fix" in action:
   212→            action_type = "auto_fix"
   213→        elif "desloppify move" in action:
   214→            action_type = "reorganize"
   215→        else:
   216→            action_type = _action_type_for_detector(detector)
   217→            # If detector says auto_fix but cluster has no fix command, it's really refactor
   218→            if action_type == "auto_fix" and "desloppify fix" not in action:
   219→                action_type = "refactor"
   220→
   221→        # Use stored description but patch the count if it differs from visible members
   222→        stored_desc = cluster_data.get("description") or ""
   223→        total_in_cluster = len(cluster_data.get("finding_ids", []))
   224→        if stored_desc and total_in_cluster != len(members):
   225→            # Replace the stored count with the visible count
   226→            summary = stored_desc.replace(str(total_in_cluster), str(len(members)))
   227→        else:
   228→            summary = stored_desc or f"{len(members)} findings"
   229→
   230→        primary_command = cluster_data.get("action")
   231→        if not primary_command:
   232→            primary_command = f"desloppify next --cluster {cname} --count 10"
   233→
   234→        meta_item: dict = {
   235→            "id": cname,
   236→            "kind": "cluster",
   237→            "action_type": action_type,
   238→            "summary": summary,
   239→            "members": members,
   240→            "member_count": len(members),
   241→            "primary_command": primary_command,
   242→            "cluster_name": cname,
   243→            "cluster_auto": True,
   244→            "confidence": "high",
   245→            "detector": detector,
   246→            "file": "",
   247→        }
   248→        result.append(meta_item)
   249→
   250→    result.sort(key=item_sort_key)
   251→    return result
   252→
   253→
   254→def build_work_queue(
   255→    state: StateModel,
   256→    *,
   257→    options: QueueBuildOptions | None = None,
   258→) -> WorkQueueResult:
   259→    """Build ranked queue items + tier metadata."""
   260→    resolved_options = options or QueueBuildOptions()
   261→
   262→    status = resolved_options.status
   263→    if status not in ALL_STATUSES:
   264→        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported status filter: {status}")
   265→    try:
   266→        subjective_threshold_value = float(resolved_options.subjective_threshold)
   267→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
   268→        subjective_threshold_value = 100.0
   269→    subjective_threshold_value = max(0.0, min(100.0, subjective_threshold_value))
   270→
   271→    finding_items = build_finding_items(
   272→        state,
   273→        scan_path=resolved_options.scan_path,
   274→        status_filter=status,
   275→        scope=resolved_options.scope,
   276→        chronic=resolved_options.chronic,
   277→    )
   278→
   279→    all_items = list(finding_items)
   280→    if (
   281→        resolved_options.include_subjective
   282→        and status in {"open", "all"}
   283→        and not resolved_options.chronic
   284→    ):
   285→        subjective_items = build_subjective_items(
   286→            state,
   287→            state.get("findings", {}),
   288→            threshold=subjective_threshold_value,
   289→        )
   290→        for item in subjective_items:
   291→            if scope_matches(item, resolved_options.scope):
   292→                all_items.append(item)
   293→
   294→    all_items.sort(key=item_sort_key)
   295→
   296→    # Apply living plan ordering if provided
   297→    if resolved_options.plan:
   298→        all_items = _apply_plan_order(
   299→            all_items,
   300→            resolved_options.plan,
   301→            include_skipped=resolved_options.include_skipped,
   302→            cluster=resolved_options.cluster,
   303→        )
   304→
   305→    # Collapse auto-clusters into meta-items (unless drilling into a cluster)
   306→    should_collapse = (
   307→        resolved_options.collapse_clusters
   308→        and resolved_options.plan
   309→        and not resolved_options.cluster
   310→        and not resolved_options.plan.get("active_cluster")
   311→    )
   312→    if should_collapse:
   313→        all_items = _collapse_clusters(all_items, resolved_options.plan)
   314→
   315→    counts = tier_counts(all_items)
   316→
   317→    requested_tier = (
   318→        int(resolved_options.tier) if resolved_options.tier is not None else None
   319→    )
   320→    selected_tier = requested_tier
   321→    fallback_reason = None
   322→    filtered = all_items
   323→
   324→    if requested_tier is not None:
   325→        filtered = [
   326→            item
   327→            for item in all_items
   328→            if _item_matches_tier(item, requested_tier)
   329→        ]
   330→        if not filtered and not resolved_options.no_tier_fallback:
   331→            chosen = choose_fallback_tier(requested_tier, counts)
   332→            if chosen is not None:
   333→                selected_tier = chosen
   334→                filtered = [
   335→                    item
   336→                    for item in all_items
   337→                    if _item_matches_tier(item, chosen)
   338→                ]
   339→                fallback_reason = (
   340→                    f"Requested T{requested_tier} has 0 open -> showing T{chosen} "
   341→                    "(nearest non-empty)."
   342→                )
   343→        elif not filtered:
   344→            fallback_reason = f"Requested T{requested_tier} has 0 open."
   345→
   346→    total = len(filtered)
   347→    if resolved_options.count is not None and resolved_options.count > 0:
   348→        filtered = filtered[: resolved_options.count]
   349→
   350→    if resolved_options.explain:
   351→        for item in filtered:
   352→            item["explain"] = item_explain(item)
   353→
   354→    available_tiers = [tier for tier, value in counts.items() if value > 0]
   355→    return {
   356→        "items": filtered,
   357→        "total": total,
   358→        "tier_counts": counts,
   359→        "requested_tier": requested_tier,
   360→        "selected_tier": selected_tier,
   361→        "fallback_reason": fallback_reason,
   362→        "available_tiers": available_tiers,
   363→        "grouped": group_queue_items(filtered, "item"),
   364→    }
   365→

    13→
    14→
    15→def make_lang_config(name: str, cfg_cls: type) -> LangConfig:
    16→    """Instantiate and validate a language config."""
    17→    try:
    18→        cfg = cfg_cls()
    19→    except (TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError, RuntimeError, OSError) as ex:
    20→        raise ValueError(
    21→            f"Failed to instantiate language config '{name}': {ex}"
    22→        ) from ex
    23→    validate_lang_contract(name, cfg)
    24→    return cfg
    25→
    26→
    27→def get_lang(name: str) -> LangConfig:
    28→    """Get a language config by name.
    29→
    30→    All plugins (full and generic) store LangConfig instances in the registry.
    31→    Test doubles that store plain classes are instantiated on demand as a fallback.
    32→    """
    33→    if not registry_state.is_registered(name):
    34→        load_all()
    35→    if not registry_state.is_registered(name):
    36→        available = ", ".join(sorted(registry_state.all_keys()))
    37→        raise ValueError(f"Unknown language: {name!r}. Available: {available}")
    38→    obj = registry_state.get(name)
    39→    if isinstance(obj, LangConfig):
    40→        return obj
    41→    return make_lang_config(name, obj)  # fallback for test doubles
    42→
    43→
    44→def auto_detect_lang(project_root: Path) -> str | None:
    45→    """Auto-detect language from project files.
    46→
    47→    When multiple config files are present (e.g. package.json + pyproject.toml),
    48→    counts actual source files to pick the dominant language instead of relying
    49→    on first-match ordering.
    50→    """
    51→    load_all()
    52→    candidates: list[str] = []
    53→    configs: dict[str, LangConfig] = {}
    54→
    55→    for lang_name, obj in registry_state.all_items():
    56→        cfg = obj if isinstance(obj, LangConfig) else make_lang_config(lang_name, obj)
    57→        configs[lang_name] = cfg
    58→        markers = getattr(cfg, "detect_markers", []) or []
    59→        if markers and any(_detect_marker_exists(project_root, marker) for marker in markers):
    60→            candidates.append(lang_name)
    61→
    62→    if not candidates:
    63→        # Marker-less fallback: pick language with most source files.
    64→        best, best_count = None, 0
    65→        for lang_name, cfg in configs.items():
    66→            count = len(cfg.file_finder(project_root))
    67→            if count > best_count:
    68→                best, best_count = lang_name, count
    69→        return best if best_count > 0 else None
    70→
    71→    if len(candidates) == 1:
    72→        return candidates[0]
    73→
    74→    # Multiple candidates: choose language with most source files.
    75→    best, best_count = None, -1
    76→    for lang_name in candidates:
    77→        count = len(configs[lang_name].file_finder(project_root))
    78→        if count > best_count:
    79→            best, best_count = lang_name, count
    80→    return best
    81→
    82→
    83→def _detect_marker_exists(project_root: Path, marker: str) -> bool:
    84→    marker_text = str(marker).strip()
    85→    if not marker_text:
    86→        return False
    87→
    88→    # Fast path for literal markers.
    89→    if (project_root / marker_text).exists():
    90→        return True
    91→
    92→    # Wildcard markers (for example "*.fsproj") are matched at project root.
    93→    if any(ch in marker_text for ch in _MARKER_GLOB_CHARS):
    94→        return any(project_root.glob(marker_text))
    95→    return False
    96→

   121→# ── Main entry point ──────────────────────────────────────
   122→
   123→
   124→def generic_lang(
   125→    name: str,
   126→    extensions: list[str],
   127→    tools: list[dict[str, Any]],
   128→    *,
   129→    exclude: list[str] | None = None,
   130→    depth: str = "shallow",
   131→    detect_markers: list[str] | None = None,
   132→    default_src: str = ".",
   133→    treesitter_spec=None,
   134→    zone_rules: list[ZoneRule] | None = None,
   135→    test_coverage_module: object | None = None,
   136→) -> LangConfig:
   137→    """Build and register a generic language plugin from tool specs.
   138→
   139→    Each entry in `tools` is::
   140→
   141→        {"label": str, "cmd": str, "fmt": str, "id": str, "tier": int,
   142→         "fix_cmd": str | None}
   143→
   144→    When ``treesitter_spec`` is provided and ``tree-sitter-language-pack`` is
   145→    installed, the plugin gains function extraction (enables duplicate
   146→    detection), and optionally import analysis (enables coupling/orphan/cycle
   147→    detection and test-coverage analysis) for no additional configuration.
   148→
   149→    Returns the built LangConfig (also registered in the language registry).
   150→    """
   151→    from desloppify.languages import register_generic_lang
   152→    from desloppify.languages._framework.base.phase_builders import (
   153→        detector_phase_security,
   154→        detector_phase_test_coverage,
   155→        shared_subjective_duplicates_tail,
   156→    )
   157→    tool_specs = normalize_tool_specs(tools, supported_formats=set(_PARSERS))
   158→
   159→    # ── Register each tool as a detector + scoring policy ──
   160→    fixers: dict[str, FixerConfig] = {}
   161→    for tool in tool_specs:
   162→        has_fixer = tool.get("fix_cmd") is not None
   163→        fixer_name = tool["id"].replace("_", "-") if has_fixer else ""
   164→        register_detector(DetectorMeta(
   165→            name=tool["id"],
   166→            display=tool["label"],
   167→            dimension="Code quality",
   168→            action_type="auto_fix" if has_fixer else "manual_fix",
   169→            guidance=f"review and fix {tool['label']} findings",
   170→            fixers=(fixer_name,) if has_fixer else (),
   171→        ))
   172→        register_scoring_policy(DetectorScoringPolicy(
   173→            detector=tool["id"],
   174→            dimension="Code quality",
   175→            tier=tool["tier"],
   176→            file_based=True,
   177→        ))
   178→        if has_fixer:
   179→            fixers[fixer_name] = make_generic_fixer(tool)
   180→
   181→    # ── Determine extractors based on tree-sitter availability ──
   182→    file_finder = make_file_finder(extensions, exclude)
   183→    extract_fn = noop_extract_functions
   184→    dep_graph_fn = empty_dep_graph
   185→    has_treesitter = False
   186→
   187→    if treesitter_spec is not None:
   188→        from desloppify.languages._framework.treesitter import is_available
   189→
   190→        if is_available():
   191→            from desloppify.languages._framework.treesitter._extractors import (
   192→                make_ts_extractor,
   193→            )
   194→            from desloppify.languages._framework.treesitter._imports import (
   195→                make_ts_dep_builder,
   196→            )
   197→
   198→            has_treesitter = True
   199→            extract_fn = make_ts_extractor(treesitter_spec, file_finder)
   200→            if treesitter_spec.import_query and treesitter_spec.resolve_import:
   201→                dep_graph_fn = make_ts_dep_builder(treesitter_spec, file_finder)
   202→
   203→    # ── Build phases: tool-specific + structural + coupling + shared ──
   204→    phases = [
   205→        make_tool_phase(t["label"], t["cmd"], t["fmt"], t["id"], t["tier"])
   206→        for t in tool_specs
   207→    ]
   208→
   209→    # Add structural phase (with AST complexity if tree-sitter available).
   210→    phases.append(_make_structural_phase(
   211→        treesitter_spec if has_treesitter else None,
   212→    ))
   213→
   214→    # Add tree-sitter-powered AST phases when available.
   215→    if has_treesitter:
   216→        from desloppify.languages._framework.treesitter.phases import (
   217→            make_ast_smells_phase,
   218→            make_cohesion_phase,
   219→            make_unused_imports_phase,
   220→        )
   221→
   222→        phases.append(make_ast_smells_phase(treesitter_spec))
   223→        phases.append(make_cohesion_phase(treesitter_spec))
   224→        if treesitter_spec.import_query:
   225→            phases.append(make_unused_imports_phase(treesitter_spec))
   226→
   227→    # Signature analysis — uses lang.extract_functions (no tree-sitter needed).
   228→    if extract_fn is not noop_extract_functions:
   229→        from desloppify.languages._framework.base.phase_builders import (
   230→            detector_phase_signature,
   231→        )
   232→
   233→        phases.append(detector_phase_signature())
   234→
   235→    phases.append(detector_phase_security())
   236→
   237→    # Add coupling phase if we have a real dep graph.
   238→    if dep_graph_fn is not empty_dep_graph:
   239→        phases.append(_make_coupling_phase(dep_graph_fn))
   240→        phases.append(detector_phase_test_coverage())
   241→
   242→    phases.extend(shared_subjective_duplicates_tail())
   243→
   244→    cfg = LangConfig(
   245→        name=name,
   246→        extensions=extensions,
   247→        exclusions=exclude or [],
   248→        default_src=default_src,
   249→        build_dep_graph=dep_graph_fn,
   250→        entry_patterns=[],
   251→        barrel_names=set(),
   252→        phases=phases,
   253→        fixers=fixers,
   254→        get_area=None,
   255→        detect_commands={
   256→            t["id"]: make_detect_fn(t["cmd"], _PARSERS[t["fmt"]])
   257→            for t in tool_specs
   258→        },
   259→        extract_functions=extract_fn,
   260→        boundaries=[],
   261→        typecheck_cmd="",
   262→        file_finder=file_finder,
   263→        large_threshold=500,
   264→        complexity_threshold=15,
   265→        default_scan_profile="objective",
   266→        detect_markers=detect_markers or [],
   267→        external_test_dirs=["tests", "test"],
   268→        test_file_extensions=extensions,
   269→        zone_rules=zone_rules if zone_rules is not None else generic_zone_rules(extensions),
   270→    )
   271→
   272→    # Set integration depth — upgrade when tree-sitter provides capabilities.
   273→    if has_treesitter and depth in ("shallow", "minimal"):
   274→        cfg.integration_depth = "standard"
   275→    else:
   276→        cfg.integration_depth = depth
   277→
   278→    # Register language-specific test coverage hooks if provided.
   279→    if test_coverage_module is not None:
   280→        from desloppify.hook_registry import register_lang_hooks
   281→
   282→        register_lang_hooks(name, test_coverage=test_coverage_module)
   283→
   284→    register_generic_lang(name, cfg)
   285→    return cfg
   286→
   287→
   288→# ── Structural + coupling phase helpers ──────────────────────
   289→
   290→
   291→def _make_structural_phase(treesitter_spec=None) -> DetectorPhase:
   292→    """Create a structural analysis phase for generic plugins."""
   293→    from desloppify.engine.detectors.base import ComplexitySignal
   294→    from desloppify.core.output import log
   295→
   296→    signals = [
   297→        ComplexitySignal(
   298→            "TODOs",
   299→            r"(?://|#|--|/\*)\s*(?:TODO|FIXME|HACK|XXX)",
   300→            weight=2,
   301→            threshold=0,
   302→        ),
   303→    ]
   304→
   305→    if treesitter_spec is not None:
   306→        from desloppify.languages._framework.treesitter import is_available
   307→
   308→        if is_available():
   309→            from desloppify.languages._framework.treesitter._complexity import (
   310→                make_callback_depth_compute,
   311→                make_cyclomatic_complexity_compute,
   312→                make_long_functions_compute,
   313→                make_max_params_compute,
   314→                make_nesting_depth_compute,
   315→            )
   316→
   317→            signals.append(ComplexitySignal(
   318→                "nesting_depth", None, weight=3, threshold=4,
   319→                compute=make_nesting_depth_compute(treesitter_spec),
   320→            ))
   321→            signals.append(ComplexitySignal(
   322→                "long_functions", None, weight=3, threshold=80,
   323→                compute=make_long_functions_compute(treesitter_spec),
   324→            ))
   325→            signals.append(ComplexitySignal(
   326→                "cyclomatic_complexity", None, weight=2, threshold=15,
   327→                compute=make_cyclomatic_complexity_compute(treesitter_spec),
   328→            ))
   329→            signals.append(ComplexitySignal(
   330→                "many_params", None, weight=2, threshold=7,
   331→                compute=make_max_params_compute(treesitter_spec),
   332→            ))
   333→            signals.append(ComplexitySignal(
   334→                "callback_depth", None, weight=2, threshold=3,
   335→                compute=make_callback_depth_compute(treesitter_spec),
   336→            ))
   337→
   338→    # God class rules (active when tree-sitter provides class extraction).
   339→    god_rules = None
   340→    has_class_query = treesitter_spec is not None and treesitter_spec.class_query
   341→    if has_class_query:
   342→        from desloppify.engine.detectors.base import GodRule
   343→
   344→        god_rules = [
   345→            GodRule("methods", "methods", lambda c: len(c.methods), 15),
   346→            GodRule("loc", "LOC", lambda c: c.loc, 500),
   347→            GodRule("attributes", "attributes", lambda c: len(c.attributes), 10),
   348→        ]
   349→
   350→    def run(path, lang):
   351→        from desloppify.languages._framework.base.shared_phases import (
   352→            run_structural_phase,
   353→        )
   354→
   355→        god_extractor_fn = None
   356→        if god_rules and has_class_query:
   357→            god_extractor_fn = _make_god_extractor(treesitter_spec, lang.file_finder)
   358→
   359→        return run_structural_phase(
   360→            path, lang,
   361→            complexity_signals=signals,
   362→            log_fn=log,
   363→            min_loc=40,
   364→            god_rules=god_rules,
   365→            god_extractor_fn=god_extractor_fn,
   366→        )
   367→
   368→    return DetectorPhase("Structural analysis", run)
   369→
   370→
   371→def _make_god_extractor(treesitter_spec, file_finder):
   372→    """Create a god-class extractor function bound to the given spec."""
   373→    def extractor(p):
   374→        return _extract_ts_classes(p, treesitter_spec, file_finder)
   375→    return extractor
   376→
   377→
   378→def _extract_ts_classes(path, treesitter_spec, file_finder):
   379→    """Extract classes with methods populated via tree-sitter.
   380→
   381→    Returns [] on any error (graceful degradation).
   382→    """
   383→    try:
   384→        from collections import defaultdict
   385→
   386→        from desloppify.languages._framework.treesitter._extractors import (
   387→            ts_extract_classes,
   388→            ts_extract_functions,
   389→        )
   390→
   391→        file_list = file_finder(path)
   392→        classes = ts_extract_classes(path, treesitter_spec, file_list)
   393→        if not classes:
   394→            return classes
   395→
   396→        functions = ts_extract_functions(path, treesitter_spec, file_list)
   397→        by_file = defaultdict(list)
   398→        for fn in functions:
   399→            by_file[fn.file].append(fn)
   400→        for cls in classes:
   401→            cls_end = cls.line + cls.loc
   402→            for fn in by_file.get(cls.file, []):
   403→                if cls.line <= fn.line <= cls_end:
   404→                    cls.methods.append(fn)
   405→
   406→        return classes
   407→    except _TS_INIT_ERRORS as exc:
   408→        logger.debug("tree-sitter class extraction failed: %s", exc)
   409→        return []
   410→
   411→
   412→def _make_coupling_phase(dep_graph_fn) -> DetectorPhase:
   413→    """Create a coupling phase for generic plugins with a dep graph."""
   414→    from desloppify.core.output import log
   415→
   416→    def run(path, lang):
   417→        from desloppify.languages._framework.base.shared_phases import (
   418→            run_coupling_phase,
   419→        )
   420→
   421→        return run_coupling_phase(
   422→            path, lang, build_dep_graph_fn=dep_graph_fn, log_fn=log,
   423→        )
   424→
   425→    return DetectorPhase("Coupling + cycles + orphaned", run)
   426→
   427→
   428→__all__ = [
   429→    "SHARED_PHASE_LABELS",
   430→    "capability_report",
   431→    "generic_lang",
   432→    "generic_zone_rules",
   433→    "make_file_finder",
   434→    "make_tool_phase",
   435→    "parse_cargo",
   436→    "parse_eslint",
   437→    "parse_gnu",
   438→    "parse_golangci",
   439→    "parse_json",
   440→    "parse_rubocop",
   441→]
   442→

   109→def _scan_root_from_files(files: list[str]) -> Path | None:
   110→    """Derive the common ancestor directory from a list of file paths."""
   111→    import os
   112→
   113→    py_files = [f for f in files if f.endswith(".py")]
   114→    if not py_files:
   115→        return None
   116→    try:
   117→        common = Path(os.path.commonpath(py_files))
   118→        return common if common.is_dir() else common.parent
   119→    except ValueError:
   120→        return None

   126→        return DetectorCoverageStatus(

   141→        if shutil.which("bandit") is not None:

   145→    def detect_lang_security_detailed(self, files, zone_map) -> LangSecurityResult:
   146→        scan_root = _scan_root_from_files(files)
   147→        if scan_root is None:

   149→

   151→

   154→        return LangSecurityResult(

   157→            coverage=coverage,

   144→def _configure_lang_runtime(
   145→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   146→    config: dict[str, object],

   151→    if not lang:

   153→
   154→    lang_options = resolve_lang_runtime_options(args, lang)
   155→    lang_settings = resolve_lang_settings(config, lang)
   156→    runtime_lang = make_lang_run(
   157→        lang,
   158→        overrides=LangRunOverrides(
   159→            review_cache=state.get("review_cache", {}),
   160→            review_max_age_days=config.get("review_max_age_days", 30),
   161→            runtime_settings=lang_settings,

   164→            props_threshold_override=config.get("props_threshold", 0),
   165→        ),
   166→    )
   167→
   168→    lang_capabilities = _state_lang_capabilities(state)
   169→    lang_capabilities[runtime_lang.name] = {
   170→        "fixers": sorted(runtime_lang.fixers.keys()),
   171→        "typecheck_cmd": runtime_lang.typecheck_cmd,
   172→    }
   173→    return runtime_lang

   176→def _reset_subjective_assessments_for_scan_reset(
   177→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   178→    *,
   179→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   180→) -> int:
   181→    """Reset known subjective dimensions to 0 so the next scan starts fresh."""
   182→    assessments = _state_subjective_assessments(state)
   183→
   184→    reset_keys = {
   185→        key.strip()
   186→        for key in assessments
   187→        if isinstance(key, str) and key.strip()
   188→    }
   189→    reset_keys.update(_subjective_reset_dimensions(lang_name=lang_name))
   190→
   191→    now = state_mod.utc_now()
   192→    for key in sorted(reset_keys):
   193→        payload = assessments.get(key)
   194→        if isinstance(payload, dict):
   195→            payload["score"] = 0.0
   196→            payload["source"] = "scan_reset_subjective"
   197→            payload["assessed_at"] = now
   198→            payload["reset_by"] = "scan_reset_subjective"
   199→            payload["placeholder"] = True
   200→            payload.pop("integrity_penalty", None)
   201→            payload.pop("components", None)
   202→            payload.pop("component_scores", None)
   203→            continue
   204→        assessments[key] = {
   205→            "score": 0.0,
   206→            "source": "scan_reset_subjective",
   207→            "assessed_at": now,
   208→            "reset_by": "scan_reset_subjective",
   209→            "placeholder": True,
   210→        }
   211→    return len(reset_keys)
   212→
   213→
   214→def _expire_provisional_manual_override_assessments(
   215→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   216→) -> int:
   217→    """Expire provisional manual-override assessments at scan start."""
   218→    assessments = _state_subjective_assessments(state)
   219→
   220→    now = state_mod.utc_now()
   221→    expired = 0
   222→    for payload in assessments.values():
   223→        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
   224→            continue
   225→        if payload.get("provisional_override") is not True:
   226→            continue
   227→        payload["score"] = 0.0
   228→        payload["source"] = "manual_override_expired"
   229→        payload["assessed_at"] = now
   230→        payload["reset_by"] = "manual_override_expired"
   231→        payload["placeholder"] = True
   232→        payload.pop("provisional_override", None)
   233→        payload.pop("provisional_until_scan", None)
   234→        payload.pop("integrity_penalty", None)
   235→        payload.pop("components", None)
   236→        payload.pop("component_scores", None)
   237→        expired += 1
   238→    return expired

   241→def prepare_scan_runtime(args) -> ScanRuntime:
   242→    """Resolve state/config/language and apply scan-time runtime settings."""
   243→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
   244→    state_file = runtime.state_path
   245→    state = runtime.state if isinstance(runtime.state, dict) else {}
   246→    state_mod.ensure_state_defaults(state)

   248→    config = runtime.config if isinstance(runtime.config, dict) else {}
   249→    lang_config = resolve_lang(args)
   250→    reset_subjective_count = 0
   251→    expired_manual_override_count = _expire_provisional_manual_override_assessments(
   252→        state
   253→    )
   254→    if getattr(args, "reset_subjective", False):
   255→        reset_subjective_count = _reset_subjective_assessments_for_scan_reset(
   256→            state,
   257→            lang_name=getattr(lang_config, "name", None),
   258→        )
   259→
   260→    include_slow = not getattr(args, "skip_slow", False)
   261→    profile = _resolve_scan_profile(getattr(args, "profile", None), lang_config)
   262→    effective_include_slow = _effective_include_slow(include_slow, profile)
   263→
   264→    lang = _configure_lang_runtime(args, config, state, lang_config)
   265→    coverage_warnings = _seed_runtime_coverage_warnings(lang)
   266→    zone_overrides_raw = config.get("zone_overrides")
   267→    zone_overrides = zone_overrides_raw if isinstance(zone_overrides_raw, dict) else None
   268→
   269→    return ScanRuntime(

   278→        effective_include_slow=effective_include_slow,
   279→        zone_overrides=zone_overrides,
   280→        reset_subjective_count=reset_subjective_count,
   281→        expired_manual_override_count=expired_manual_override_count,
   282→        coverage_warnings=coverage_warnings,
   283→    )
   284→
   285→
   286→def _augment_with_stale_exclusion_findings(
   287→    findings: list[dict[str, Any]],
   288→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   289→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   290→    """Append stale exclude findings when excluded dirs are unreferenced."""
   291→    extra_exclusions = get_exclusions()
   292→    if not (extra_exclusions and runtime.lang and runtime.lang.file_finder):
   293→        return findings
   294→
   295→    scanned_files = runtime.lang.file_finder(runtime.path)
   296→    stale = _audit_excluded_dirs(
   297→        extra_exclusions, scanned_files, PROJECT_ROOT
   298→    )
   299→    if not stale:
   300→        return findings
   301→
   302→    augmented = list(findings)
   303→    augmented.extend(stale)
   304→    for stale_finding in stale:
   305→        print(colorize(f"  ℹ {stale_finding['summary']}", "dim"))
   306→    return augmented
   307→
   308→
   309→def _augment_with_stale_wontfix_findings(
   310→    findings: list[dict[str, Any]],
   311→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   312→    *,
   313→    decay_scans: int,
   314→) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], int]:
   315→    """Append re-triage findings for stale/worsening wontfix debt."""
   316→    return _augment_stale_wontfix_impl(
   317→        findings,
   318→        state=runtime.state,
   319→        scan_path=runtime.path,
   320→        project_root=PROJECT_ROOT,
   321→        decay_scans=decay_scans,
   322→    )
   323→
   324→
   325→def run_scan_generation(
   326→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   327→) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, object], dict[str, object] | None]:
   328→    """Run detector pipeline and return findings, potentials, and codebase metrics."""
   329→    from desloppify.languages._framework.treesitter import (
   330→        disable_parse_cache,
   331→        enable_parse_cache,
   332→    )
   333→
   334→    enable_file_cache()
   335→    enable_parse_cache()
   336→    try:
   337→        findings, potentials = plan_mod.generate_findings(
   338→            runtime.path,
   339→            lang=runtime.lang,
   340→            options=PlanScanOptions(
   341→                include_slow=runtime.effective_include_slow,
   342→                zone_overrides=runtime.zone_overrides,
   343→                profile=runtime.profile,
   344→            ),
   345→        )
   346→    finally:
   347→        disable_parse_cache()
   348→        disable_file_cache()
   349→
   350→    codebase_metrics = _collect_codebase_metrics(runtime.lang, runtime.path)
   351→    _warn_explicit_lang_with_no_files(
   352→        runtime.args, runtime.lang, runtime.path, codebase_metrics
   353→    )
   354→    findings = _augment_with_stale_exclusion_findings(findings, runtime)
   355→    decay_scans = _coerce_int(
   356→        runtime.config.get("wontfix_decay_scans"),
   357→        default=_WONTFIX_DECAY_SCANS_DEFAULT,
   358→    )
   359→    findings, monitored_wontfix = _augment_with_stale_wontfix_findings(
   360→        findings,
   361→        runtime,
   362→        decay_scans=max(decay_scans, 0),
   363→    )
   364→    potentials["stale_wontfix"] = monitored_wontfix
   365→    return findings, potentials, codebase_metrics
   366→
   367→
   368→def merge_scan_results(
   369→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   370→    findings: list[dict[str, Any]],
   371→    potentials: dict[str, object],
   372→    codebase_metrics: dict[str, object] | None,
   373→) -> ScanMergeResult:
   374→    """Merge findings into persistent state and return diff + previous score snapshot."""
   375→    scan_path_rel = rel(str(runtime.path))
   376→    prev_scan_path = runtime.state.get("scan_path")
   377→    path_changed = prev_scan_path is not None and prev_scan_path != scan_path_rel
   378→
   379→    if not path_changed:
   380→        prev = state_mod.score_snapshot(runtime.state)
   381→    else:
   382→        prev = state_mod.ScoreSnapshot(None, None, None, None)
   383→    prev_dim_scores = (
   384→        runtime.state.get("dimension_scores", {}) if not path_changed else {}
   385→    )
   386→
   387→    if runtime.lang and runtime.lang.zone_map is not None:
   388→        runtime.state["zone_distribution"] = runtime.lang.zone_map.counts()
   389→    _persist_scan_coverage(runtime.state, runtime.lang)
   390→
   391→    target_score = target_strict_score_from_config(runtime.config, fallback=95.0)
   392→
   393→    diff = state_mod.merge_scan(
   394→        runtime.state,
   395→        findings,
   396→        options=state_mod.MergeScanOptions(
   397→            lang=runtime.lang.name if runtime.lang else None,
   398→            scan_path=scan_path_rel,
   399→            force_resolve=getattr(runtime.args, "force_resolve", False),
   400→            exclude=get_exclusions(),
   401→            potentials=potentials,
   402→            codebase_metrics=codebase_metrics,
   403→            include_slow=runtime.effective_include_slow,
   404→            ignore=runtime.config.get("ignore", []),
   405→            subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   406→        ),
   407→    )
   408→
   409→    issues_mod.expire_stale_holistic(
   410→        runtime.state, runtime.config.get("holistic_max_age_days", 30)
   411→    )
   412→    state_mod.save_state(
   413→        runtime.state,
   414→        runtime.state_path,
   415→        subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   416→    )
   417→
   418→    # Clear needs_rescan flag after successful scan merge (best-effort)
   419→    if runtime.config.get("needs_rescan"):
   420→        try:
   421→            runtime.config["needs_rescan"] = False
   422→            _save_config(runtime.config)
   423→        except OSError:
   424→            pass
   425→
   426→    # Reconcile living plan + sync stale subjective dimensions
   427→    try:
   428→        from desloppify.engine.plan import (
   429→            load_plan,
   430→            reconcile_plan_after_scan,
   431→            save_plan,
   432→            sync_stale_dimensions,
   433→            sync_unscored_dimensions,
   434→        )
   435→
   436→        plan_path = runtime.state_path.parent / "plan.json" if runtime.state_path else None
   437→        plan = load_plan(plan_path)
   438→        dirty = False
   439→
   440→        # Standard reconciliation (only if plan has user content)
   441→        if (
   442→            plan.get("queue_order")
   443→            or plan.get("overrides")
   444→            or plan.get("clusters")
   445→            or plan.get("skipped")
   446→        ):
   447→            recon = reconcile_plan_after_scan(plan, runtime.state)
   448→            if recon.changes:
   449→                dirty = True
   450→            if recon.resurfaced:
   451→                print(colorize(
   452→                    f"  Plan: {len(recon.resurfaced)} skipped item(s) re-surfaced after review period.",
   453→                    "cyan",
   454→                ))
   455→
   456→        # Unscored dimension sync (prepend to front, unconditional)
   457→        unscored_sync = sync_unscored_dimensions(plan, runtime.state)
   458→        if unscored_sync.changes:
   459→            dirty = True
   460→        if unscored_sync.injected:
   461→            print(colorize(
   462→                f"  Plan: {len(unscored_sync.injected)} unscored subjective dimension(s) queued for initial review.",
   463→                "cyan",
   464→            ))
   465→
   466→        # Stale dimension sync (always — handles both cleanup and injection)
   467→        dim_sync = sync_stale_dimensions(plan, runtime.state)
   468→        if dim_sync.changes:
   469→            dirty = True
   470→        if dim_sync.pruned:
   471→            print(colorize(
   472→                f"  Plan: {len(dim_sync.pruned)} refreshed subjective dimension(s) removed from queue.",
   473→                "cyan",
   474→            ))
   475→        if dim_sync.injected:
   476→            print(colorize(
   477→                f"  Plan: {len(dim_sync.injected)} stale subjective dimension(s) queued for refresh.",
   478→                "cyan",
   479→            ))
   480→
   481→        # Auto-cluster findings into task groups
   482→        from desloppify.engine._plan.auto_cluster import auto_cluster_findings
   483→
   484→        ac_changes = auto_cluster_findings(plan, runtime.state)
   485→        if ac_changes:
   486→            dirty = True
   487→
   488→        if dirty:
   489→            save_plan(plan, plan_path)
   490→    except Exception:
   491→        pass  # Plan reconciliation is best-effort
   492→
   493→    return ScanMergeResult(
   494→        diff=diff,
   495→        prev_overall=prev.overall,
   496→        prev_objective=prev.objective,
   497→        prev_strict=prev.strict,
   498→        prev_verified=prev.verified,
   499→        prev_dim_scores=prev_dim_scores,
   500→    )
   501→
   502→
   503→def resolve_noise_snapshot(
   504→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   505→    config: dict[str, object],
   506→) -> ScanNoiseSnapshot:
   507→    """Resolve noise budget settings and hidden finding counters."""
   508→    noise_budget, global_noise_budget, budget_warning = (
   509→        state_mod.resolve_finding_noise_settings(config)
   510→    )
   511→    findings_by_id = _state_findings(state)
   512→    open_findings = [
   513→        finding
   514→        for finding in state_mod.path_scoped_findings(
   515→            findings_by_id, state.get("scan_path")
   516→        ).values()
   517→        if finding.get("status") == "open"
   518→    ]
   519→    _, hidden_by_detector = state_mod.apply_finding_noise_budget(
   520→        open_findings,
   521→        budget=noise_budget,
   522→        global_budget=global_noise_budget,
   523→    )
   524→
   525→    return ScanNoiseSnapshot(
   526→        noise_budget=noise_budget,
   527→        global_noise_budget=global_noise_budget,
   528→        budget_warning=budget_warning,
   529→        hidden_by_detector=hidden_by_detector,
   530→        hidden_total=sum(hidden_by_detector.values()),
   531→    )
   532→
   533→
   534→def persist_reminder_history(
   535→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   536→    narrative: dict[str, object],
   537→) -> None:
   538→    """Persist reminder history emitted by narrative computation."""
   539→    if not (narrative and "reminder_history" in narrative):
   540→        return
   541→
   542→    runtime.state["reminder_history"] = narrative["reminder_history"]
   543→    target_score = target_strict_score_from_config(runtime.config, fallback=95.0)
   544→    state_mod.save_state(
   545→        runtime.state,
   546→        runtime.state_path,
   547→        subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   548→    )
   549→
   550→
   551→__all__ = [
   552→    "ScanStateContractError",

   558→    "prepare_scan_runtime",
   559→    "resolve_noise_snapshot",

1→"""Text-oriented utility helpers split from the main utils facade."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import os
     6→from pathlib import Path
     7→
     8→_DEFAULT_PROJECT_ROOT = Path(os.environ.get("DESLOPPIFY_ROOT", Path.cwd())).resolve()
     9→
    10→# Legacy module-level constant — kept for backwards compat, but prefer
    11→# get_project_root() which respects RuntimeContext overrides.
    12→PROJECT_ROOT = _DEFAULT_PROJECT_ROOT
    13→
    14→
    15→def get_project_root() -> Path:
    16→    """Return the active project root, checking RuntimeContext first.
    17→
    18→    Tests set ``RuntimeContext.project_root`` to point at a tmp directory.
    19→    Production code uses the process-level default from $DESLOPPIFY_ROOT / cwd.
    20→    """
    21→    from desloppify.core.runtime_state import current_runtime_context
    22→
    23→    override = current_runtime_context().project_root
    24→    if override is not None:
    25→        return override
    26→    return _DEFAULT_PROJECT_ROOT
    27→
    28→
    29→def read_code_snippet(
    30→    filepath: str,
    31→    line: int,
    32→    context: int = 1,
    33→    *,
    34→    project_root: Path | str | None = None,
    35→) -> str | None:
    36→    """Read ±context lines around a line number. Returns formatted string or None."""
    37→    try:
    38→        root = (
    39→            Path(project_root).resolve()
    40→            if project_root is not None
    41→            else PROJECT_ROOT
    42→        )
    43→        full = Path(filepath)
    44→        if not full.is_absolute():
    45→            full = root / full
    46→        content = full.read_text(errors="replace")
    47→    except OSError:
    48→        return None
    49→    lines = content.splitlines()
    50→    if line < 1 or line > len(lines):
    51→        return None
    52→    start = max(0, line - 1 - context)
    53→    end = min(len(lines), line + context)
    54→    parts = []
    55→    for i in range(start, end):
    56→        ln = i + 1
    57→        marker = "→" if ln == line else " "
    58→        text = lines[i]
    59→        if len(text) > 120:
    60→            text = text[:117] + "..."
    61→        parts.append(f"    {marker} {ln:>4} │ {text}")
    62→    return "\n".join(parts)
    63→
    64→
    65→def get_area(filepath: str, *, min_depth: int = 2) -> str:
    66→    """Derive an area name from a file path (generic: first 2 path components).
    67→
    68→    *min_depth* controls the minimum number of path components required before
    69→    the two-component area is returned.  The default (2) means a path like
    70→    ``"a/b"`` already qualifies.  Python uses ``min_depth=3`` so that
    71→    ``"pkg/mod.py"`` returns just ``"pkg"`` while ``"pkg/sub/mod.py"`` returns
    72→    ``"pkg/sub"``.
    73→    """
    74→    text = (filepath or "").strip()
    75→    if not text:
    76→        return "(unknown)"
    77→    parts = Path(text).parts
    78→    if not parts:
    79→        return "(unknown)"
    80→    return "/".join(parts[:2]) if len(parts) >= min_depth else parts[0]
    81→
    82→
    83→def strip_c_style_comments(text: str) -> str:
    84→    """Strip // and /* */ comments while preserving string literals."""
    85→    result: list[str] = []
    86→    i = 0
    87→    in_str = None
    88→    while i < len(text):
    89→        ch = text[i]
    90→        if in_str:
    91→            if ch == "\\" and i + 1 < len(text):
    92→                result.append(text[i : i + 2])
    93→                i += 2
    94→                continue
    95→            if ch == in_str:
    96→                in_str = None
    97→            result.append(ch)
    98→            i += 1
    99→        elif ch in ('"', "'", "`"):
   100→            in_str = ch
   101→            result.append(ch)
   102→            i += 1
   103→        elif ch == "/" and i + 1 < len(text):
   104→            if text[i + 1] == "/":
   105→                nl = text.find("\n", i)
   106→                if nl == -1:
   107→                    break
   108→                i = nl
   109→            elif text[i + 1] == "*":
   110→                end = text.find("*/", i + 2)
   111→                if end == -1:
   112→                    break
   113→                i = end + 2
   114→            else:
   115→                result.append(ch)
   116→                i += 1
   117→        else:
   118→            result.append(ch)
   119→            i += 1
   120→    return "".join(result)
   121→
   122→
   123→def is_numeric(value: object) -> bool:
   124→    """Return True if *value* is an int or float but NOT a bool.
   125→
   126→    Python's ``bool`` is a subclass of ``int``, so ``isinstance(True, int)``
   127→    is ``True``.  Many JSON-derived payloads need to distinguish real numbers
   128→    from booleans; this helper centralises that guard.
   129→    """
   130→    return isinstance(value, int | float) and not isinstance(value, bool)
   131→
   132→
   133→__all__ = [
   134→    "PROJECT_ROOT",
   135→    "get_area",
   136→    "get_project_root",
   137→    "is_numeric",
   138→    "read_code_snippet",
   139→    "strip_c_style_comments",
   140→]
   141→

    90→def default_config() -> dict[str, Any]:
    91→    """Return a config dict with all keys set to their defaults."""
    92→    return {k: copy.deepcopy(v.default) for k, v in CONFIG_SCHEMA.items()}

    94→
    95→def _coerce_target_strict_score(value: object) -> tuple[int, bool]:
    96→    """Coerce target strict score and report whether it is in range."""
    97→    try:
    98→        parsed = int(value)
    99→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
   100→        return MIN_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE, False
   101→    valid = MIN_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE <= parsed <= MAX_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE
   102→    return parsed, valid
   103→
   104→
   105→def load_config(path: Path | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
   106→    """Load config from disk, auto-migrating from state files if needed.
   107→
   108→    Fills missing keys with defaults. If no config.json exists, attempts
   109→    migration from state-*.json files.
   110→    """
   111→    p = path or CONFIG_FILE
   112→    if p.exists():
   113→        try:
   114→            config = json.loads(p.read_text())
   115→        except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
   116→            config = {}
   117→    else:
   118→        # First run — try migrating from state files
   119→        config = _migrate_from_state_files(p)
   120→
   121→    changed = False
   122→
   123→    # Fill missing keys with defaults
   124→    for key, schema in CONFIG_SCHEMA.items():
   125→        if key not in config:
   126→            config[key] = copy.deepcopy(schema.default)
   127→            changed = True
   128→        elif key == "badge_path":
   129→            try:
   130→                normalized = _validate_badge_path(str(config[key]))
   131→                if normalized != config[key]:
   132→                    config[key] = normalized
   133→                    changed = True
   134→            except ValueError:
   135→                config[key] = copy.deepcopy(schema.default)
   136→                changed = True
   137→
   138→    if changed and p.exists():
   139→        try:
   140→            save_config(config, p)
   141→        except OSError as exc:
   142→            log_best_effort_failure(logger, f"persist migrated config to {p}", exc)
   143→
   144→    return config
   145→
   146→
   147→def save_config(config: dict, path: Path | None = None) -> None:
   148→    """Save config to disk atomically."""
   149→    p = path or CONFIG_FILE
   150→    safe_write_text(p, json.dumps(config, indent=2) + "\n")
   151→
   152→
   153→def add_ignore_pattern(config: dict, pattern: str) -> None:
   154→    """Append a pattern to the ignore list (deduplicates)."""
   155→    ignores = config.setdefault("ignore", [])
   156→    if pattern not in ignores:
   157→        ignores.append(pattern)
   158→
   159→
   160→def add_exclude_pattern(config: dict, pattern: str) -> None:
   161→    """Append a pattern to the exclude list (deduplicates)."""
   162→    excludes = config.setdefault("exclude", [])
   163→    if pattern not in excludes:
   164→        excludes.append(pattern)
   165→
   166→
   167→def set_ignore_metadata(config: dict, pattern: str, *, note: str, added_at: str) -> None:
   168→    """Record note + timestamp for an ignore pattern."""
   169→    meta = config.setdefault("ignore_metadata", {})
   170→    if not isinstance(meta, dict):
   171→        meta = {}
   172→        config["ignore_metadata"] = meta
   173→    meta[pattern] = {"note": note, "added_at": added_at}
   174→
   175→
   176→def _validate_badge_path(raw: str) -> str:
   177→    """Require badge_path to point to a filename (root or nested path)."""
   178→    value = raw.strip()
   179→    path = Path(value)
   180→    if (
   181→        not value
   182→        or value.endswith(("/", "\\"))
   183→        or path.name in {"", ".", ".."}
   184→    ):
   185→        raise ValueError(
   186→            "Expected file path for badge_path "
   187→            f"(example: scorecard.png or assets/scorecard.png), got: {raw}"
   188→        )
   189→    return value
   190→
   191→
   192→def set_config_value(config: dict, key: str, raw: str) -> None:
   193→    """Parse and set a config value from a raw string.
   194→
   195→    Handles special cases:
   196→    - "never" → 0 for age keys
   197→    - "true"/"false" for bools
   198→    """
   199→    if key not in CONFIG_SCHEMA:
   200→        raise KeyError(f"Unknown config key: {key}")
   201→
   202→    schema = CONFIG_SCHEMA[key]
   203→
   204→    if schema.type is int:
   205→        if raw.lower() == "never":
   206→            config[key] = 0
   207→        else:
   208→            config[key] = int(raw)
   209→        if key == "target_strict_score":
   210→            target_strict_score, target_valid = _coerce_target_strict_score(config[key])
   211→            if not target_valid:
   212→                raise ValueError(
   213→                    f"Expected integer {MIN_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE}-{MAX_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE} "
   214→                    f"for {key}, got: {raw}"
   215→                )
   216→            config[key] = target_strict_score
   217→    elif schema.type is bool:
   218→        if raw.lower() in ("true", "1", "yes"):
   219→            config[key] = True
   220→        elif raw.lower() in ("false", "0", "no"):
   221→            config[key] = False
   222→        else:
   223→            raise ValueError(f"Expected true/false for {key}, got: {raw}")
   224→    elif schema.type is str:
   225→        if key == "badge_path":
   226→            config[key] = _validate_badge_path(raw)
   227→        else:
   228→            config[key] = raw
   229→    elif schema.type is list:
   230→        # For list keys, append the value
   231→        config.setdefault(key, [])
   232→        if raw not in config[key]:
   233→            config[key].append(raw)
   234→    elif schema.type is dict:
   235→        raise ValueError(f"Cannot set dict key '{key}' via CLI — use subcommands")
   236→    else:
   237→        config[key] = raw
   238→
   239→
   240→def unset_config_value(config: dict, key: str) -> None:
   241→    """Reset a config key to its default value."""
   242→    if key not in CONFIG_SCHEMA:
   243→        raise KeyError(f"Unknown config key: {key}")
   244→    config[key] = copy.deepcopy(CONFIG_SCHEMA[key].default)

   246→
   247→def config_for_query(config: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
   248→    """Return a sanitized config dict suitable for query.json."""
   249→    return {k: config.get(k, schema.default) for k, schema in CONFIG_SCHEMA.items()}
   250→
   251→
   252→def _merge_config_value(config: dict, key: str, value: object) -> None:
   253→    """Merge a config value into the target dict."""
   254→    if key not in config:
   255→        config[key] = copy.deepcopy(value)
   256→        return
   257→    if isinstance(value, list) and isinstance(config[key], list):
   258→        for item in value:
   259→            if item not in config[key]:
   260→                config[key].append(item)
   261→        return
   262→    if isinstance(value, dict) and isinstance(config[key], dict):
   263→        for dk, dv in value.items():
   264→            if dk not in config[key]:
   265→                config[key][dk] = copy.deepcopy(dv)
   266→        return
   267→
   268→def _migrate_from_state_files(config_path: Path) -> dict:
   269→    """Migrate config keys from state-*.json files into config.json.
   270→
   271→    Reads state["config"] from all state files, merges them (union for
   272→    lists, merge for dicts), writes config.json, and strips "config" from
   273→    the state files.
   274→    """
   275→    config: dict = {}
   276→    state_dir = config_path.parent
   277→    if not state_dir.exists():
   278→        return config
   279→
   280→    state_files = list(state_dir.glob("state-*.json")) + list(
   281→        state_dir.glob("state.json")
   282→    )
   283→    migrated_any = False
   284→    for sf in state_files:
   285→        try:
   286→            state_data = json.loads(sf.read_text())
   287→        except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, OSError) as exc:
   288→            logger.debug("Skipping unreadable state file %s: %s", sf, exc)
   289→            continue
   290→
   291→        old_config = state_data.get("config")
   292→        if not old_config or not isinstance(old_config, dict):
   293→            continue
   294→
   295→        # Merge: union for lists, merge for dicts, first-wins for scalars
   296→        for k, v in old_config.items():
   297→            if k not in CONFIG_SCHEMA:
   298→                continue
   299→            _merge_config_value(config, k, v)
   300→
   301→        # Strip "config" from state file
   302→        if "config" in state_data:
   303→            del state_data["config"]
   304→            try:
   305→                safe_write_text(sf, json.dumps(state_data, indent=2) + "\n")
   306→            except OSError as exc:
   307→                log_best_effort_failure(
   308→                    logger,
   309→                    f"rewrite state file {sf} after config migration",
   310→                    exc,
   311→                )
   312→
   313→        migrated_any = True
   314→
   315→    if migrated_any and config:
   316→        try:
   317→            save_config(config, config_path)
   318→        except OSError as exc:
   319→            log_best_effort_failure(
   320→                logger, f"save migrated config to {config_path}", exc
   321→            )
   322→
   323→    return config
   324→

1→"""Language registry: plugin registration and language resolution."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import inspect
     6→from collections.abc import Callable
     7→from pathlib import Path
     8→from typing import TypeVar
     9→
    10→from desloppify.languages._framework import (
    11→    discovery,
    12→    registry_state,
    13→    resolution,
    14→    runtime,
    15→)
    16→from desloppify.languages._framework.base.types import LangConfig
    17→from desloppify.languages._framework.contract_validation import validate_lang_contract
    18→from desloppify.languages._framework.policy import REQUIRED_DIRS, REQUIRED_FILES
    19→from desloppify.languages._framework.resolution import (
    20→    auto_detect_lang,
    21→    available_langs,
    22→    get_lang,
    23→    make_lang_config,
    24→)
    25→from desloppify.languages._framework.structure_validation import validate_lang_structure
    26→
    27→T = TypeVar("T")
    28→
    29→
    30→def register_lang(name: str) -> Callable[[T], T]:
    31→    """Decorator to register a language config class.
    32→
    33→    Validates structure, instantiates the class, validates the contract,
    34→    and stores the *instance* in the registry.
    35→    """
    36→
    37→    def decorator(cls: T) -> T:
    38→        module = inspect.getmodule(cls)
    39→        if module and hasattr(module, "__file__"):
    40→            validate_lang_structure(Path(module.__file__).parent, name)
    41→        if isinstance(cls, type) and issubclass(cls, LangConfig):
    42→            cfg = make_lang_config(name, cls)  # instantiate + validate
    43→            registry_state.register(name, cfg)  # store instance
    44→        else:
    45→            registry_state.register(name, cls)  # test doubles
    46→        return cls
    47→
    48→    return decorator
    49→
    50→
    51→def register_generic_lang(name: str, cfg: LangConfig) -> None:
    52→    """Register a pre-built language plugin instance (no package structure required)."""
    53→    validate_lang_contract(name, cfg)
    54→    registry_state.register(name, cfg)
    55→
    56→
    57→__all__ = [
    58→    "REQUIRED_FILES",
    59→    "REQUIRED_DIRS",
    60→    "register_lang",
    61→    "register_generic_lang",
    62→    "get_lang",
    63→    "available_langs",
    64→    "auto_detect_lang",
    65→    "make_lang_config",
    66→    "validate_lang_structure",
    67→    "validate_lang_contract",
    68→    "discovery",
    69→    "registry_state",

    71→    "runtime",
    72→]

1→"""Runtime contract validation for LangConfig plugins."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.languages._framework.base.types import (
     6→    DetectorPhase,
     7→    FixerConfig,
     8→    LangConfig,
     9→    LangValueSpec,
    10→)
    11→from desloppify.languages._framework.policy import ALLOWED_SCAN_PROFILES
    12→
    13→
    14→def _validate_core_identity(name: str, cfg: LangConfig) -> list[str]:
    15→    errors: list[str] = []
    16→    if cfg.name != name:
    17→        errors.append(f"config name mismatch: expected '{name}', got '{cfg.name}'")
    18→    if not cfg.extensions:
    19→        errors.append("extensions must be non-empty")
    20→    if not callable(cfg.build_dep_graph):
    21→        errors.append("build_dep_graph must be callable")
    22→    if not callable(cfg.file_finder):
    23→        errors.append("file_finder must be callable")
    24→    if not callable(cfg.extract_functions):
    25→        errors.append("extract_functions must be callable")
    26→    if cfg.default_scan_profile not in ALLOWED_SCAN_PROFILES:
    27→        allowed = ", ".join(sorted(ALLOWED_SCAN_PROFILES))
    28→        errors.append(f"default_scan_profile must be one of: {allowed}")
    29→    return errors
    30→
    31→
    32→def _validate_phases(cfg: LangConfig) -> list[str]:
    33→    errors: list[str] = []
    34→    if not cfg.phases:
    35→        errors.append("phases must be non-empty")
    36→        return errors
    37→
    38→    for idx, phase in enumerate(cfg.phases):
    39→        if not isinstance(phase, DetectorPhase):
    40→            errors.append(f"phase[{idx}] is not DetectorPhase")
    41→            continue
    42→        if not isinstance(phase.label, str) or not phase.label.strip():
    43→            errors.append(f"phase[{idx}] has empty label")
    44→        if not callable(phase.run):
    45→            errors.append(f"phase[{idx}] run must be callable")
    46→    return errors
    47→
    48→
    49→def _validate_detect_commands(cfg: LangConfig) -> list[str]:
    50→    errors: list[str] = []
    51→    if not isinstance(cfg.detect_commands, dict) or not cfg.detect_commands:
    52→        errors.append("detect_commands must be a non-empty dict")
    53→        return errors
    54→
    55→    for key, fn in cfg.detect_commands.items():
    56→        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key.strip():
    57→            errors.append("detect_commands has empty/non-string key")
    58→        elif (
    59→            key != key.lower()
    60→            or "-" in key
    61→            or not all(ch.isalnum() or ch == "_" for ch in key)
    62→        ):
    63→            errors.append(f"detect command '{key}' must use lowercase snake_case")
    64→        if not callable(fn):
    65→            errors.append(f"detect command '{key}' is not callable")
    66→    return errors
    67→
    68→
    69→def _validate_fixers(cfg: LangConfig) -> list[str]:
    70→    errors: list[str] = []
    71→    if not isinstance(cfg.fixers, dict):
    72→        errors.append("fixers must be a dict")
    73→        return errors
    74→
    75→    for key, fixer in cfg.fixers.items():
    76→        if not isinstance(fixer, FixerConfig):
    77→            errors.append(f"fixer '{key}' is not FixerConfig")
    78→    return errors
    79→
    80→
    81→def _validate_setting_specs(cfg: LangConfig) -> list[str]:
    82→    errors: list[str] = []
    83→    if not isinstance(cfg.setting_specs, dict):
    84→        errors.append("setting_specs must be a dict")
    85→        return errors
    86→
    87→    for key, spec in cfg.setting_specs.items():
    88→        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key.strip():
    89→            errors.append("setting_specs has empty/non-string key")
    90→        if not isinstance(spec, LangValueSpec):
    91→            errors.append(f"setting_specs['{key}'] is not LangValueSpec")
    92→    return errors
    93→
    94→
    95→def _validate_runtime_option_specs(cfg: LangConfig) -> list[str]:
    96→    errors: list[str] = []
    97→    if not isinstance(cfg.runtime_option_specs, dict):
    98→        errors.append("runtime_option_specs must be a dict")
    99→        return errors
   100→
   101→    for key, spec in cfg.runtime_option_specs.items():
   102→        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key.strip():
   103→            errors.append("runtime_option_specs has empty/non-string key")
   104→        if not isinstance(spec, LangValueSpec):
   105→            errors.append(f"runtime_option_specs['{key}'] is not LangValueSpec")
   106→    return errors
   107→
   108→
   109→def _validate_zone_rules(cfg: LangConfig) -> list[str]:
   110→    return [] if cfg.zone_rules else ["zone_rules must be non-empty"]
   111→
   112→
   113→def validate_lang_contract(name: str, cfg: LangConfig) -> None:
   114→    """Validate LangConfig runtime contract so broken plugins fail fast."""
   115→    errors: list[str] = []
   116→
   117→    if not isinstance(cfg, LangConfig):
   118→        errors.append(f"plugin class for '{name}' must return LangConfig")
   119→    else:
   120→        errors.extend(_validate_core_identity(name, cfg))
   121→        errors.extend(_validate_phases(cfg))
   122→        errors.extend(_validate_detect_commands(cfg))
   123→        errors.extend(_validate_fixers(cfg))
   124→        errors.extend(_validate_setting_specs(cfg))
   125→        errors.extend(_validate_runtime_option_specs(cfg))
   126→        errors.extend(_validate_zone_rules(cfg))
   127→
   128→    if errors:
   129→        raise ValueError(
   130→            f"Language plugin '{name}' has invalid LangConfig contract:\n"
   131→            + "\n".join(f"  - {e}" for e in errors)
   132→        )
   133→

    90→        if not isinstance(spec, LangValueSpec):
    91→            errors.append(f"setting_specs['{key}'] is not LangValueSpec")
    92→    return errors
    93→
    94→
    95→def _validate_runtime_option_specs(cfg: LangConfig) -> list[str]:
    96→    errors: list[str] = []
    97→    if not isinstance(cfg.runtime_option_specs, dict):
    98→        errors.append("runtime_option_specs must be a dict")
    99→        return errors
   100→
   101→    for key, spec in cfg.runtime_option_specs.items():
   102→        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key.strip():
   103→            errors.append("runtime_option_specs has empty/non-string key")
   104→        if not isinstance(spec, LangValueSpec):
   105→            errors.append(f"runtime_option_specs['{key}'] is not LangValueSpec")
   106→    return errors
   107→
   108→
   109→def _validate_zone_rules(cfg: LangConfig) -> list[str]:
   110→    return [] if cfg.zone_rules else ["zone_rules must be non-empty"]
   111→
   112→
   113→def validate_lang_contract(name: str, cfg: LangConfig) -> None:
   114→    """Validate LangConfig runtime contract so broken plugins fail fast."""
   115→    errors: list[str] = []
   116→
   117→    if not isinstance(cfg, LangConfig):
   118→        errors.append(f"plugin class for '{name}' must return LangConfig")
   119→    else:
   120→        errors.extend(_validate_core_identity(name, cfg))
   121→        errors.extend(_validate_phases(cfg))
   122→        errors.extend(_validate_detect_commands(cfg))
   123→        errors.extend(_validate_fixers(cfg))
   124→        errors.extend(_validate_setting_specs(cfg))
   125→        errors.extend(_validate_runtime_option_specs(cfg))
   126→        errors.extend(_validate_zone_rules(cfg))
   127→
   128→    if errors:
   129→        raise ValueError(
   130→            f"Language plugin '{name}' has invalid LangConfig contract:\n"
   131→            + "\n".join(f"  - {e}" for e in errors)
   132→        )
   133→

    36→def make_dupe_findings(entries: list[dict], stderr_fn) -> list[Finding]:

    56→                f"{a['name']} ({rel(a['file'])}:{a['line']}), "

    90→def make_single_use_findings(
    91→    entries: list[dict],
    92→    get_area,
    93→    *,
    94→    loc_range: tuple[int, int] = (50, 200),
    95→    suppress_colocated: bool = True,
    96→    skip_dir_names: set[str] | None = None,
    97→    stderr_fn,
    98→) -> list[Finding]:
    99→    """Filter and normalize single-use entries into findings.
   100→
   101→    Suppresses entries within the LOC range (they're appropriately-sized abstractions),
   102→    entries co-located with their sole importer, and entries in skip_dir_names
   103→    directories (e.g., commands/ -- CLI modules are single-use by design).
   104→    """
   105→    results = []
   106→    colocated_suppressed = 0
   107→    lo, hi = loc_range
   108→    for e in entries:
   109→        if lo <= e["loc"] <= hi:
   110→            continue
   111→        # Skip files in directories that are single-use by design (e.g., commands/)
   112→        if skip_dir_names:
   113→            parts = Path(e["file"]).parts
   114→            if any(p in skip_dir_names for p in parts):
   115→                continue
   116→        if suppress_colocated and get_area:
   117→            src_area = get_area(rel(e["file"]))
   118→            imp_area = get_area(e["sole_importer"])
   119→            if src_area == imp_area:
   120→                colocated_suppressed += 1
   121→                continue
   122→        results.append(
   123→            make_finding(
   124→                "single_use",
   125→                e["file"],
   126→                "",
   127→                tier=3,
   128→                confidence="medium",
   129→                summary=f"Single-use ({e['loc']} LOC): only imported by {e['sole_importer']}",
   130→                detail={"loc": e["loc"], "sole_importer": e["sole_importer"]},
   131→            )
   132→        )
   133→    suppressed = len(entries) - len(results)
   134→    coloc_note = f", {colocated_suppressed} co-located" if colocated_suppressed else ""
   135→    stderr_fn(
   136→        f"         single-use: {len(entries)} found, {suppressed} suppressed "
   137→        f"({lo}-{hi} LOC{coloc_note})"

     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→
     7→from desloppify.languages._framework.policy import REQUIRED_DIRS, REQUIRED_FILES

     9→
    10→def validate_lang_structure(lang_dir: Path, name: str) -> None:
    11→    """Validate that a language plugin has all required files and directories."""
    12→    errors: list[str] = []
    13→
    14→    for filename in REQUIRED_FILES:
    15→        if not (lang_dir / filename).is_file():
    16→            errors.append(f"missing required file: {filename}")
    17→
    18→    for dirname in REQUIRED_DIRS:
    19→        target = lang_dir / dirname
    20→        if not target.is_dir():
    21→            errors.append(f"missing required directory: {dirname}/")
    22→            continue
    23→        if not (target / "__init__.py").is_file():
    24→            errors.append(f"missing {dirname}/__init__.py")
    25→        if dirname == "tests" and not any(target.glob("test_*.py")):
    26→            errors.append("tests directory must contain at least one test_*.py file")
    27→
    28→    if errors:
    29→        raise ValueError(
    30→            f"Language plugin '{name}' ({lang_dir.name}/) has structural issues:\n"
    31→            + "\n".join(f"  - {e}" for e in errors)
    32→        )
    33→

    55→class _TreeDetectorSpec:
    56→    smell_id: str
    57→    collect: TreeCollector
    58→
    59→
    60→_NodeCollectorNoTree = Callable[[str, ast.AST], list[SmellMatch]]
    61→_NodeCollectorWithTree = Callable[[str, ast.AST, ast.Module], list[SmellMatch]]
    62→
    63→
    64→class _TreeDetectorWithNodesKw(Protocol):
    65→    """Tree detector accepting `all_nodes` as an optional keyword argument."""
    66→
    67→    def __call__(
    68→        self,
    69→        filepath: str,
    70→        tree: ast.Module,
    71→        *,
    72→        all_nodes: tuple[ast.AST, ...] | None = None,
    73→    ) -> list[SmellMatch]: ...
    74→
    75→
    76→def _node_without_tree(collector: _NodeCollectorNoTree) -> NodeCollector:
    77→    """Adapt node collectors that don't use the AST module object."""
    78→
    79→    def _collect(filepath: str, node: ast.AST, tree: ast.Module) -> list[SmellMatch]:
    80→        del tree
    81→        return collector(filepath, node)
    82→
    83→    return _collect
    84→
    85→
    86→def _node_with_tree(collector: _NodeCollectorWithTree) -> NodeCollector:
    87→    """Keep collector signatures explicit when tree context is required."""
    88→    return collector
    89→
    90→
    91→def _tree_with_optional_nodes_kw(collector: _TreeDetectorWithNodesKw) -> TreeCollector:
    92→    """Adapt tree collectors expecting `all_nodes=` keyword parameter."""
    93→
    94→    def _collect(
    95→        filepath: str,
    96→        tree: ast.Module,
    97→        all_nodes: tuple[ast.AST, ...] | None,
    98→    ) -> list[SmellMatch]:
    99→        return collector(filepath, tree, all_nodes=all_nodes)
   100→
   101→    return _collect
   102→
   103→
   104→def _import_boundary_collector(smell_id: str) -> TreeCollector:
   105→    """Build an explicit tree collector for one import-boundary smell id."""
   106→
   107→    def _collect(
   108→        filepath: str,
   109→        tree: ast.Module,
   110→        all_nodes: tuple[ast.AST, ...] | None,
   111→    ) -> list[SmellMatch]:
   112→        return _detect_import_time_boundary_mutations(
   113→            filepath,
   114→            tree,
   115→            smell_id=smell_id,
   116→            all_nodes=all_nodes,
   117→        )
   118→
   119→    return _collect

   225→
   226→def _detect_ast_smells(filepath: str, content: str, smell_counts: dict[str, list]):
   227→    """Detect AST-based code smells using registry-driven collector dispatch."""
   228→    try:
   229→        tree = ast.parse(content)
   230→    except SyntaxError:
   231→        return
   232→
   233→    # Build a single-walk context index for node-level detectors.
   234→    all_nodes = tuple(ast.walk(tree))
   235→    fn_nodes = tuple(
   236→        node
   237→        for node in all_nodes
   238→        if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef)
   239→    )
   240→
   241→    for spec in NODE_DETECTORS:
   242→        matches: list[SmellMatch] = []
   243→        for fn_node in fn_nodes:
   244→            matches.extend(spec.collect(filepath, fn_node, tree))
   245→        merge_smell_matches(smell_counts, spec.smell_id, matches)
   246→
   247→    for spec in TREE_DETECTORS:
   248→        matches = spec.collect(filepath, tree, all_nodes)
   249→        merge_smell_matches(smell_counts, spec.smell_id, matches)
   250→

   332→def on_detector_registered(callback: Callable[[], None]) -> None:

   337→def register_detector(meta: DetectorMeta) -> None:
   338→    """Register a detector at runtime (used by generic plugins)."""
   339→    global JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   340→    DETECTORS[meta.name] = meta
   341→    if meta.name not in _DISPLAY_ORDER:
   342→        _DISPLAY_ORDER.append(meta.name)
   343→    JUDGMENT_DETECTORS = frozenset(
   344→        name for name, m in DETECTORS.items() if m.needs_judgment
   345→    )
   346→    for cb in _on_register_callbacks:
